For a broad class of symmetric heavy-tailed gradient noise distributions, we show that the proposed estimator has a finite second moment even when the underlying gradient noise has an infinite second moment. For nonconvex objectives, this yields convergence to a neighborhood of zero in expected squared gradient norm at a rate of $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1})$. We explicitly characterize the size of this neighborhood in terms of the noise and algorithm parameters. When the time horizon $T$ is known in advance, we establish an $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1/2})$ convergence rate. A diminishing step size achieves the same rate up to a logarithmic factor. Incorporating clipping or a more general nonlinear transformation yields high-probability convergence guarantees with the same rate up to logarithmic factors. Experimental results indicate that R-SGD-Mini and its clipped or nonlinear variant consistently perform favorably compared to SGD, clipped SGD, Nonlinear SGD and Median-of-Means based methods.

papers.title: The clumsy coupon collector's problem
papers.abstract: We consider a generalisation of the classical coupon collector's problem, in which at each time step a collector either receives a new copy of a randomly chosen coupon, or loses all their previously collected copies of that coupon. We consider the amount of time it takes this clumsy coupon collector to obtain the full set of $m$ coupons. We establish limit theorems as $m\to\infty$ for the clumsy coupon collection time, and describe the large $m$ asymptotics of its mean and variance. We identify three regimes, depending on how the probability of a clumsy update, $p$, scales with $m$. If $p=o(1/m)$, we obtain a Gumbel limit theorem, as is the case for the classical coupon collector. If $p=ω(1/m)$, we instead show weak convergence to an exponential random variable. In the critical case, $p\sim c/m$, we give a full characterisation of the limiting distribution in terms of a birth-and-death process. We also describe the asymptotics of the mean and variance in these three regimes.

papers.title: A Mathematical Characterization of Neural Activation Induced by Temporal Interference Stimulation
papers.abstract: Temporal Interference Stimulation (TIS) is a non-invasive neuromodulation technique in which two high-frequency sinusoidal currents with slightly different frequencies generate a low-frequency envelope that can activate deep neural structures. This study investigates the conditions under which TIS elicits action potentials in a single neuron modeled by the FitzHugh-Nagumo system. This research integrates phase-plane analysis and geometric singular perturbation to develop a mathematical framework for analyzing TIS. By combining a mathematical analysis of differential equations with computer simulations, the study elucidates how the amplitudes and beat frequency jointly determine whether the neuron remains quiescent, exhibits only transient responses, or undergoes persistent (tonic) firing.

papers.title: A quasi-orthogonal method based on the inverse operator for Schrödinger eigenvalue problems
papers.abstract: The simultaneous computation of many Schrödinger eigenpairs requires mutually orthogonal eigenfunctions. We propose a quasi-orthogonal evolution model based on the inverse operator and a two-stage time discretization for nonorthogonal initial data. The continuous trajectory and discrete iterates remain full rank and approach orthogonality without any orthogonalization. The discretization preserves the current Gram matrix in the first stage and reduces the orthogonality error in the second. We establish well-posedness, energy decay, asymptotic orthogonality, and exponential convergence to the target eigenfunctions up to fixed orthogonal transformations. Numerical experiments for two Schr{ö}dinger eigenvalue problems validate the decay of the energy, gradient norm, and relative iterate error, while the iterates become numerically orthogonal. Further experiments show that the discrete time steps remain effective under mesh refinement, that convergence rates depend on the spectral gap, and that dynamically adjusting the solve accuracy can accelerate the computation.

papers.title: Logarithmic oscillatory multipliers and log-subdyadic square functions
papers.abstract: We develop square-function estimates for Fourier multipliers whose local oscillation scale is \[ ρ(R)=\frac{R}{(\log R)^{γ-1}}, \qquad γ>1. \] This scale lies strictly between the dyadic scale and every fixed power-subdyadic scale at high frequency. For high-frequency symbols satisfying a localized Sobolev condition on balls of radius comparable to $ρ(R)$, we prove a pointwise square-function estimate and a weighted $L^2$ multiplier inequality. After adjoining a smooth compactly supported low-frequency part, we derive unweighted $L^p$ bounds. The weighted estimate is governed by a logarithmic geometric maximal operator which is strongly bounded above the critical $L^r$ threshold, satisfies weak type at the critical equality, and fails even weak type below it. As a model application, consider \[ L(ξ)=\frac12\log(e^2+|ξ|^2), \qquad m_{γ,β}(ξ)=L(ξ)^{-β}e^{iL(ξ)^γ}. \] For $p=2$, the associated multiplier is bounded on $L^2$ for every $β\geq0$. For $1<p<\infty$, $p\neq2$, it is bounded on $L^p$ under the sufficient condition \[ β> d(γ-1)\left|\frac12-\frac1p\right|. \] At the critical equality we obtain the corresponding Lorentz endpoint estimates.

papers.title: Discrete approximation of semi-Dirichlet forms with non-symmetric perturbations of resistance forms
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study discrete approximations of semi-Dirichlet forms obtained by adding non-symmetric drift terms, expressed in terms of mutual energy measures, to resistance forms whose associated resistance metric spaces are compact. The main novelty is that the drift terms need not to be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Under suitable smallness assumptions, we prove generalized Mosco convergence of the approximating forms and derive weak convergence of the associated Feller processes. We also demonstrate the applicability of our main theorem to post-critically finite self-similar fractals and describe the resulting perturbation of the approximating jump chains in the case of the Sierpiński gasket.

papers.title: Accelerating Sinkhorn for Entropy-Regularized Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Entropy-regularized optimal transport is widely used to compare and align data distributions, but Sinkhorn can converge slowly at small regularization. We introduce Acc-Sinkhorn, a two-state Hessian-driven Nesterov iteration built on the dual mirror geometry of the row-reduced Sinkhorn map. The method combines momentum acceleration with an inexpensive descent safeguard, stable log-domain evaluation, and a prescribed homotopy schedule requiring neither line search nor curvature estimation. We prove global linear convergence of the safeguarded method, rule out consecutive restarts, and establish local accelerated convergence for fixed parameters without restarts through spectral analysis. Numerical comparisons with six methods on synthetic problems, color transfer, and bilingual word alignment show runtime speedups of up to about 26 over Sinkhorn, with additional rendering-accuracy comparisons for color transfer.

papers.title: Cyclic source pairings for Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor spaces
papers.abstract: We determine the stable source information carried by the gluing-groupoid algebra of the Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor double. Relative normal residues define supported analytic $K$-classes with specified normal orientations. For a smooth double along a closed submanifold, we compute the full geometric periodic cyclic homology as the parity sum of the compactly supported cohomologies of the ambient manifold and the doubled locus. In the physical model, $K_0\cong\Z^4$ and $HP_0\cong\C^4$, with both odd groups zero. Four explicit cocycles give integral $K$-coordinates and exhaust continuous periodic cyclic cohomology; every periodic cyclic pairing on supported source classes is therefore a linear combination of rank and degree. Finite moments recover $K$-valued normal profiles modulo integral common line twists. A first-jet criterion tests mixed-line triviality and identifies the residue with the torsion cokernel of a generically invertible second fundamental form for pullback quotients. The degree-one Euler modification and the diagonal Coulomb embedding have identical filtered $K$-profiles in every algebraic $SL_2$ representation, while their rank-two Ward connections are respectively indecomposable and split. We give the Euler connection and its transition between both root charts. An elementary holonomy realization shows that the inherited ambient and divisor transverse classes annihilate supported source classes. The relative degree pairing uses an additional choice of opposite defect orientations.
papers.comments: 43 pages. v2 substantially revised and extended. Source classes now use relative normal residues and supported Thom induction; the quadratic common-twist claim is corrected. Adds analytic K-theory and periodic cyclic computations (supported pairings reduce to rank and degree), filtered profiles, mixed-line criteria, an explicit Euler ASD connection and a foliation realization

papers.title: Large-time behavior and accuracy of the Mean-Field Ensemble Kalman Filter in the Linear Detectable Setting
papers.abstract: The ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF), originally developed in the geophysical sciences, is now widely used for state and parameter estimation problems in various domains of application, and in particular in high dimensional settings. It may be viewed as a robust, cheap-to-implement,alternative to the optimal, Bayesian, filter. However, despite its empirical successes, theoretical understanding of its properties, in relation to the optimal filter, is in its infancy. We contribute novel theoretical understanding, studying the behavior of the EnKF in the infinite particle number setting; this is known as the mean-field ensemble Kalman filter (MFEnKF). In the linear setting with Gaussian noise and Gaussian initial data the MFEnKF coincides with the optimal filter, which is characterized by the Kalman filter. Our focus in this paper will be the linear setting with Gaussian noise, but with non-Gaussian initial data. Under the assumptions of nondegeneracy of the signal noise and detectability of the signal-observation pair we make three specific contributions, studying both discrete and continuous formulations of the methodology. First, in discrete time, we derive the MFEnKF via a variational approximation of the Bayes update using a covariance-weighted optimal transport metric. Secondly, we use this metric to show that the MFEnKF is a strict contraction towards the subspace of Gaussian measures, giving explicit geometric rates in terms of the covariances, in both discrete and continuous time. Finally, in the continuous-time setting, we deduce a stable form of almost sure accuracy of the MFEnKF: given any pair of initial laws (satisfying mild conditions) for the MFEnKF and the optimal filter, the 2-Wasserstein distance between their distributions decays exponentially, for almost every observation path.

papers.title: A closed subspace of a Gateaux differentiability space is a Gateaux differentiability space : over 46 years of open problem solved
papers.abstract: This paper establishes, for the first time, an iterative and rigid theory of weak\(^{*}\) slices in a non-metric setting, demonstrating that dual convex sets admit localization, diameter control and fine structural analysis under the pure weak\(^{*}\) topology. It fundamentally reshapes the classical perspective on the geometric features of the weak\(^{*}\) topology and thereby pioneers a new direction in non-metric weak\(^{*}\) slice geometry. Using a novel technique built upon intricate manipulation of weak\(^{*}\) slices and a carefully engineered iterative selection scheme, we prove that if $M$ is a closed subspace of a G$\mathrm{\hat{a}}$teaux differentiability space $X$, then $M$ itself is a G$\mathrm{\hat{a}}$teaux differentiability space. As a corollary, we obtain that if $X$ is a weak Asplund space and $M$ is a closed subspace of $X$, then $M$ is a G$\mathrm{\hat{a}}$teaux differentiability space. This settles definitively an open problem posed 46 years ago by D.G. Larman and R.R. Phelps (J. London Math. Soc., 20 (1979), 115-127).

papers.title: Simplicity of q-Gaussian C*-algebras
papers.abstract: We show that q-Gaussian $C^*$-algebras for $q \in (-1, 1)$ have the Dixmier averaging property, and hence are simple with a unique trace. We argue by combining rapid decay and spectral gap estimates for the commutators with the generators, which are obtained from free probability.
papers.comments: Final version; to appear in Bulletin of LMS

papers.title: Rank Recursion for $q$-Whittaker and Macdonald Operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and prove a set of rank recurrence relations for $q$-Whittaker and Macdonald operators. We also derive an explicit expression for the $k$-th power of the $q$-Whittaker operators in terms of the $q$-deformed binomial probability distribution, and we express the rank recurrence relations for the Macdonald operators in terms of the Cauchy determinant.
papers.comments: 30 pages, corrections for q-Whittaker power identity and proof. Comments are welcome!

papers.title: On a local variant of the 12th Delfino problem -- the $Π$-side
papers.abstract: Assume that \(M_n\), the canonical inner model with \(n\) Woodin cardinals, exists, where \(1\leq n<ω\). We force a cardinal-preserving extension of \(M_n\) in which CH holds and the reals have a lightface \(Δ^1_{n+3}\) wellorder. In this extension \(\bfΣ^1_{n+3}\)-separation holds and rules out every good \(\bfΔ^1_{n+3}\) wellorder of the reals. Every boldface \(\bfΣ^1_{n+2}\) set of reals is Lebesgue measurable and has the Baire property, and \(\bfΠ^1_{n+1}\)-determinacy fails. Thus the regularity and wellorder at the levels suggested by \(M_{n+1}\) can already be obtained by forcing over \(M_n\). For odd \(n\), \(\bfΔ^1_{n+1}\)-determinacy also fails. Hence for odd \(n\geq3\) we answer the adjacent-level Friedman--Schindler question negatively, while for even \(n\geq2\) we answer its \(Π\)-determinacy variant negatively. We prove in \(\ZFC\) that for every \(k\geq2\), a \(\bfΔ^1_k\) wellorder of the reals precludes \(\bfΠ^1_k\)-reduction. Hence \(\bfΠ^1_{n+3}\)-reduction and \(\bfΠ^1_{n+3}\)-uniformization fail in our extension.
papers.comments: This repairs the previous version whose main result turned out to be too strong

papers.title: Optimized high-order IMEX-RK schemes for degenerate diffusion-reaction problems with application to travelling waves phenomena
papers.abstract: We study a class of IMplicit-EXplicit Runge--Kutta (IMEX-RK) schemes for the numerical approximation of reaction and diffusion-reaction problems arising in a variety of biological and physical applications. Such models may admit travelling wave solutions, with the Fisher--Kolmogorov equation representing a prototypical example. Motivated by this feature, the proposed time integration schemes are designed to accurately capture sharp propagating fronts. We also investigate a less standard use of IMEX-RK methods that circumvents a splitting of reaction terms into linear and nonlinear components, while still requiring the solution of linear systems at each stage. This semi-implicit formulation, referred to as SI-IMEX-RK, enables a targeted treatment of stiffness by isolating its relevant contributions. The time discretization is coupled with a high-order polygonal discontinuous Galerkin method for space discretization, resulting in a flexible and robust framework for the treatment of multiscale dynamics in complex geometries. A comprehensive validation strategy is presented to assess the accuracy and stability properties of the proposed schemes across a hierarchy of increasingly challenging test problems.

papers.title: Polynomial valuations on plane polygons
papers.abstract: Scissors congruence problems involving translations have prompted the study of translation invariant simple valuations. We review this classical theory from a naive and consistent viewpoint: starting from a description of all simple valuations on polygons, we characterize the effect of translation invariance. A description of all polynomial simple valuations is obtained as a bi-product of the adopted approach and as a direct generalization of the translation invariant theory; it appears to be new.

papers.title: Computing canonical labellings of finite solvable groups
papers.abstract: We define a canonical labelling function on the class of finite solvable groups so that two such groups $G$ and $H$ are isomorphic if and only if can$(G)=$can$(H)$. Specifically, can$(G)$ is a group presentation that describes a group isomorphic to $G$, and our description explains how to construct an isomorphism $G\to$can$(G)$. Our approach is motivated by O'Brien's (1993) canonical presentations for finite $p$-groups and utilises ideas from group cohomology first described by Robinson (1982) and automorphism group algorithms developed by Smith (1994), Holt (2001), and others. We also discuss a proof-of-concept implementation for the computer algebra system GAP and comment on the major bottlenecks and open research questions.

papers.title: On triviality and scalar curvature estimation of gradient $h$-almost Yamabe solitons
papers.abstract: In this study we have explored gradient $h$-almost Yamabe solitons on both compact and complete non-compact Riemannian manifolds. We have established several sufficient conditions for the triviality of such solitons with respect to integral inequalities involving the scalar curvature and the soliton function. In this regard, we have acquired scalar curvature estimation under certain $L^1$ and $L^2$ integrability conditions, and defined signal of the function $h$. Our results extend and refine former works on almost and $h$-almost Yamabe solitons, and characterize the geometric structures of generalized Yamabe solitons.

papers.title: Local solutions to hyperbolic systems with fractional dissipation
papers.abstract: We study the local Cauchy problem for a class of hyperbolic quasilinear evolution systems with fractional dissipation and commutators of the fractional Laplacian $(-Δ)^α$ with arbitrary $α\in(0,1)$ in the framework of Sobolev spaces. The analysis is motivated by the compressible Euler alignment system with singular communication weights. We show that the contribution of the commutators to the energy is absorbed by the dissipation. Our approach does not rely on the cancellation condition previously used to recover the coercivity of the highest order nonlocal terms. We further show that the commutator term induces a loss of regularity in the stability estimates, preventing the standard contraction argument from being applied. Therefore, we instead establish the relative compactness of the solution operator and apply Schauder's fixed point theorem to provide local existence for large initial data. The resulting theory identifies the obstacles to deduce local uniqueness in the presence of commutators.

papers.title: $L^p$-form of the KNRS conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a graph with $m>0$ edges and $n$ non-isolated vertices. For every $ρ$-locally dense graphon $W$, we prove that $\|W_F\|_q\geρ^m$ whenever $q\ge\binom n2/m$, where $W_F$ is the product of $W$ over the edges of $F$. The KNRS conjecture asks for this bound at $q=1$. More generally, averaging over the automorphisms of an edge-transitive KNRS supergraph $J$ yields the sufficient exponent $e(J)/m$; for $ρ>0$ and $q>e(J)/m$, equality holds only for constant graphons. The proof averages over vertex relabellings via Hölder's inequality, in the spirit of Conlon and Lee. We also prove that replacing every edge of a Sidorenko-good graph by a fixed theta pattern preserves goodness for all branch lengths, and that applying the same substitution to a KNRS graph yields a regular-KNRS graph. For non-uniform substitutions, we establish goodness under the branch-count conditions of Im, Li, and Liu and determine when equality forces the kernel to be constant. Passing to the one-subdivision recovers their theorem for even branch lengths.

papers.title: A nine-line counterexample to a conjecture on the minimal degree of Jacobian relations
papers.abstract: We construct two arrangements of nine lines in the complex projective plane with isomorphic intersection lattices, of weak combinatorics $(n_2,n_3,n_4)=(9,7,1)$, whose defining equations $f$ and $g$ satisfy $${\rm mdr}(f)=4,\qquad {\rm mdr}(g)=5.$$ Since $4<9/2$, this disproves a conjecture of the first author which would have implied Terao's Conjecture on the combinatorial nature of the freeness of line arrangements. Equivalently, the rank two vector bundle of logarithmic vector fields is strictly semistable for the first arrangement and stable for the second one. Hence the stability of this bundle is not determined by the intersection lattice, which gives a counterexample to a conjecture of Abe. The two arrangements also have different minimal free resolutions of their Milnor algebras. All computations are exact, and a short SINGULAR script performing them is included.
papers.comments: 9 pages, this is a final version incorporating referee's remarks, and it contains a new result which is a counterexample to Abe's conjecture, to appear in European Journal of Mathematics

papers.title: The Insertion List-Decoding Capacity and an Improved Bound on the Deletion List-Decoding Capacity
papers.abstract: Informally, the capacity of list-decoding in a given adversarial error model is the largest rate at which we can list-decode with list size polynomial in the block length. The capacity of list-decoding from insertions and deletions is a basic, yet poorly understood, aspect of coding against synchronization errors. For example, when dealing with a $δ>1/2$ fraction of insertions, the best known lower bounds give little more than the fact that the capacity is positive. Beyond that regime we also only have loose bounds, with the lower bounds stemming from the analysis of uniformly random codes. We make progress in our understanding of the limits of list-decoding binary codes from insertions and deletions. We show that the capacity of list-decoding from a $δ$-fraction of insertions is exactly \begin{equation*} (1+δ)\left(1-h\left(\fracδ{1+δ}\right)\right) \end{equation*} for all $δ\in[0,1]$, where $h$ is the binary entropy function, achieved with high probability by a code sampled according to a symmetric $2$-state Markov chain. Curiously, we complement this by showing that such an approach does not beat uniformly random coding in list-decoding from deletions. We also give an improved upper bound on the capacity of list-decoding from a $δ$-fraction of deletions, showing in particular that it behaves like $1-h(δ)+o(δ)$ when $δ\to 0$. This matches the first-order asymptotic behavior of the capacity of the binary deletion channel for vanishing deletion probability, but differs in the second-order term.
papers.comments: 25 pages. A preliminary version of this work appears in ITCS 2027

papers.title: Homological Topological Quantum Field Theories
papers.abstract: We develop a new framework for quantum invariants of $3$-manifolds by extending to cobordisms a homological construction of mapping class group representations. More specifically, we construct a $(2+1)$-dimensional topological quantum field theory (TQFT) that assigns to each surface the twisted homology of its unordered configuration space. The construction requires a choice of local systems on configuration spaces together with additional data. We formulate sufficient conditions on these data that guarantee the TQFT axioms, and we show that there are at least two useful examples satisfying them. One of them yields a homological construction of the projective Kerler--Lyubashenko TQFT, while the other recovers the Frohman--Nicas--Donaldson TQFT. In contrast to the classical algebraic constructions of quantum invariants, our approach is purely topological and relies on multi-trajectory spaces of cobordisms.
papers.comments: 61 pages. Revised version. Corrected a coefficient hypothesis and revised Morse compatibility to use left and right locality. Clarified handle maps on small cycles, corrected the Schroedinger coefficient maps, and gave the degreewise normalization for the monoidal De Renzi--Martel comparison. The main conclusions are unchanged. The additional claim of a Hermitian TQFT has been withdrawn

papers.title: Higher-power inverse functional identities and Frobenius collision obstructions
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a division ring, let $n\geq 2$, and let $f,g:D\to D$ be additive maps satisfying $f(x)x^{-1}+x^n g(x^{-1})=0$ for every nonzero $x\in D$. We establish general vanishing criteria, give an explicit classification over finite fields, and determine the additive-polynomial solutions over infinite fields of positive characteristic. If $\mathbb{F}_q\subseteq Z(D)$, every additive map $D\to D$ admits a canonical decomposition into $\mathbb{F}_q^\times$-weight components, and the identity pairs precisely the weights $r,s$ satisfying $r+s\equiv n+1\pmod{q-1}$. Consequently, for $q=p^m$, the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of the solution space is the number of ordered pairs $(i,j)$ with $0\leq i,j<m$ satisfying $p^i+p^j\equiv n+1\pmod{q-1}$. Over an infinite field of characteristic $p>0$, the additive-polynomial solutions are exactly the sums of paired Frobenius terms with $p^i+p^j=n+1$. This classification concerns additive-polynomial maps and does not assert a classification of arbitrary additive maps. Prime-field dilation gives complete vanishing in characteristic zero and, in characteristic $p>0$, whenever $p-1$ does not divide $n-1$. In characteristic two, we prove complete vanishing for $n=2$ on every noncommutative division ring. More generally, when $[D:Z(D)]=\infty$, every solution vanishes if the center is infinite. If the center is the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, the same conclusion holds for $2\leq n\leq q-1$. The remaining cases are stated explicitly.
papers.comments: Now 23 pages. Some typos have been corrected, and Remark 3.14 has been added
papers.journal_ref: Journal of Algebra Combinatorics Discrete Structures and Applications (2026)

papers.title: Graph-Induced Rotational Twisted States in Systems of Identical Oscillators
papers.abstract: In this article, we study a new class of collective motion for identical coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators on graphs. This model was previously known to converge to the synchronized state for a certain class of initial data. Here, we show that when the interaction matrix is circulant, there exists another class of attractors, in which the particles are uniformly distributed on a circle, reminiscent of the \textit{twisted states} known for the Kuramoto model, but which rotate around the origin. However, contrary to the classical Kuramoto case, here the rotation is caused by the asymmetry of the graph structure, and not by the natural frequencies. We identify conditions for the existence and local stability of the \textit{rotational twisted states}, both in the Stuart-Landau model and in the Kuramoto model. We also provide sufficient conditions for the existence and stability of the synchronized state, which can co-exist with the rotational twisted state in a certain parameter region. We provide a generalization of the class of interaction matrices able to generate rotational twisted states via leader-follower interaction matrices. We show that heterogeneous rotational twisted states can also exist for a system of heterogeneous oscillators, attracted to different individual target amplitudes. This study is accompanied by numerical simulations that illustrate the possible behaviors of the system, which also include metastable dynamics and a chimera state.

papers.title: CORTET: Robust generation of simulation-ready tetrahedral meshes of the fetal cerebral cortex
papers.abstract: Every human brain folds differently, and such natural variation confounds the search for imaging biomarkers of neurodevelopmental disorders. Physics-based simulation can help determine the causal mechanisms that underpin this variability. Yet every simulation must be initiated from a volumetric mesh of the brain's interior, tetrahedral or hexahedral, and it is the worst element in that mesh, not the average, that decides whether the simulation runs at all. Building that mesh from fetal MRI currently requires labour-intensive manual intervention. We therefore present CORTET (CORtical TETrahedral meshing): a fully automated pipeline that converts a triangulated cortical surface into a solver-ready tetrahedral mesh whose worst-element quality meets a strict quality target with no manual repair. By benchmarking against a general-purpose tetrahedral mesher on the same input surfaces, we isolate the pipeline's contribution from that of the input geometry, and we validate quality across a cohort of nearly 200 fetal subjects spanning the folding period. A mesh taken straight from the pipeline sustains a numerically stable morphoelastic folding simulation of a real fetal subject.

papers.title: Punctured Wilson--Evolving Sets and Root Identities for Massive Kirchhoff Forests
papers.abstract: Let $F_q$ be the rooted forest sampled by Wilson's algorithm for a finite reversible Markov chain killed at rate $q$. We express the probability that $k$ prescribed vertices are roots as a product. For the $i$th factor, start an evolving set from the singleton consisting of the $i$th vertex, in the domain obtained by removing the preceding $i-1$ vertices. The factor is the probability that the set contains its starting vertex at an independent exponential time of rate $q$. These factors are the successive Schur-complement pivots of the determinantal root kernel. The construction couples the walk up to its exit from a domain with the evolving set biased by its mass. For the ordinary evolving set, the expected mass at that time divided by the initial mass is the probability that the walk has not yet left the domain. We use the probability that a second walk hits the first Wilson branch to bound the probability that two vertices belong to the same component. For a symmetric transition kernel, the expected size of the component of any vertex is at most $(1+1/q)^2$. Under a Gaussian heat-kernel upper bound with exponent $ν>4$, we also obtain spatial decay on the scale $q^{-1/2}$, up to a finite-volume correction.

papers.title: A Markov duration model with power-law decay via level-slope matching
papers.abstract: We develop a two-dimensional Markov duration model with power-law rate decay and a flexible residual distribution. The two state variables specify the excitation level and decay scale of a single power-law rate curve, and each update matches the level and slope jumps of a power-law Hawkes intensity. Under a sufficient stability condition, a finite residual mean, and a positive continuous residual density, the state at event times is positive Harris recurrent and converges geometrically in total variation to a unique invariant distribution. With unit exponential residuals, the sufficient region contains every parameter value for which the matched Hawkes process is subcritical. We apply the model to E-mini S\&P 500 futures and NVDA midquote durations at several price-change thresholds. Flexible residual laws improve likelihood-based fit, and power-law decay lowers one-step negative log predictive scores relative to exponential decay. An autoregressive conditional duration model generally leaves less residual autocorrelation, while forecast rankings vary with the price threshold and evaluation criterion.
papers.comments: Updated the title, revised the model formulation and stability proofs, and added an empirical study of financial durations

papers.title: Pathwise Uniqueness for Cyclically Catalytic Branching Diffusions
papers.abstract: We study pathwise uniqueness for cyclic catalytic stochastic differential equations whose state-dependent square-root diffusion coefficients are non-Lipschitz and degenerate on the boundary. The approach is the direct construction of a strong solution using a Malliavin compactness criterion. The key is the development of a new family of boundary-sensitive weighted Malliavin estimates for the tangent processes of the smooth approximations. Pathwise uniqueness then follows from the dual Yamada-Watanabe argument together with the weak uniqueness available in the literature.

papers.title: Edge State Propagation Near Multiple and Singular Interfaces
papers.abstract: We study the semiclassical propagation of edge-states for a two-dimensional Dirac operator with a spatially varying mass. The zero set of the mass models the interface between topological phases and is allowed either to consist of two disjoint smooth curves or to possess an isolated singular point. For disjoint interfaces, we prove that a wave packet initially localized on one component remains confined near this interface over long semiclassical time scales and we quantify the influence of the distance between the two components on the accuracy of the approximation. For singular interfaces, we determine the regime in which the wave-packet approximation remains valid as the packet approaches the singularity and identify the scaling at which our estimates lose their uniformity.

papers.title: Eigenvalues of the tetradiagonal Toeplitz matrices with diagonals 1, 0, 0, 1
papers.abstract: We perform a thorough analysis of the eigenvalues of tetradiagonal Toeplitz matrices of large order $n$ generated by the Laurent polynomial $a(t)=t^2+t^{-1}$. The spectra of these matrices are invariant under $2π/3$-rotation. They are contained in three segments of the complex plane and asymptotically fill these segments as $n$ tends to infinity. We apply Widom's formula for the determinants and transform the characteristic equation into a convenient form that can be solved by the fixed point iteration method. The main results are asymptotic formulas for the eigenvalues, both close to the origin and far from the origin. The main results are verified by numerical tests for moderate values of $n$.
papers.comments: 45 pages, 14 figures; more bibliographic references are added in version 2

papers.title: Nonnuclear Bunce-Deddens algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce nonnuclear Bunce-Deddens algebras, defined as reduced crossed product C*-algebras associated with free odometer actions of nonamenable countable discrete residually finite groups on a Cantor space. These are nonnuclear counterparts to the generalised Bunce-Deddens algebras introduced by Orfanos. For large classes of groups, we show that they share many regularity properties, including real rank zero, stable rank one, strict comparison of positive elements, and admitting a unique tracial state. In many cases, we deduce that they are even selfless and hence pure. Finally, we compute the ordered K-theory and trace pairing of Bunce-Deddens algebras over nonabelian free groups.
papers.comments: 17 pages, 1 figure. Incorporated changes suggested by the anonymous referee, resulting in a strengthening of Theorem B and simplified proof of real rank zero. To appear in Münster J. Math

papers.title: An Orlicz variational formula for David-type Beltrami equations
papers.abstract: We develop a Banach-space variational theory for degenerate Beltrami equations of David type. For coefficients supported in a bounded domain $\mathcal{U}\subset\mathbb{C}$, the pointwise change of variables $ν=2μ/(1-|μ|^2)$ identifies the David coefficients with the exponential Orlicz space $L^Φ_{\mathcal{U}}(\mathbb{C})$ for $Φ(s)=e^s-s-1$. On the open subset of parameters with a sufficiently large exponential moment, the principal solution map is locally real $C^{1,1}$ into $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{C})$, with Fréchet derivative solving the linearized Beltrami equation. On the Orlicz heart $E^Φ_{\mathcal{U}}(\mathbb{C})$ it is real $C^\infty$, yet fails to be real analytic at zero: along any direction $h$, its Taylor series at zero has radius of convergence $1/\|h\|_\infty$ in $W^{1,2}(B)$ for every disk $B\supset\overline{\mathcal{U}}$. Finally, for $\mathcal{U}=\mathbb{D}$, the exterior Schwarzian map from $E^Φ_{\mathbb{D}}(\mathbb{C})$ to the little logarithmic Bers space is continuous, but fails to be Fréchet differentiable at zero; moreover, its zero fiber is not a $C^1$ embedded Banach submanifold near zero, obstructing any local $C^1$ split submersion structure on the resulting quotient.

papers.title: Local and global invertibility of pluriharmonic mappings
papers.abstract: We prove a higher-dimensional Kneser theorem for pluriharmonic maps on bounded Stein domains whose closures are topological manifolds with boundary. A homeomorphism on the boundary and containment in the target domain imply a homeomorphism of the closures and a real-analytic diffeomorphism of the interiors. We classify pluriharmonic homeomorphisms between round shells in $\C^n$ for $n\ge2$. Such maps exist exactly when the two inner-to-outer radius ratios agree, and each is the restriction of a centered real similarity. We also prove the local Lewy theorem in every complex dimension: local injectivity is equivalent to a nonvanishing real Jacobian. For smooth boundary data, a formula counts the critical points of each real scalar projection with their holomorphic multiplicities. The boundary criterion gives removability for maps on punctured domains. For bounded pluriharmonic maps of controlled distortion, we obtain Lipschitz estimates on bounded $C^2$ domains in complex dimension at least two. For quasiconformal pluriharmonic homeomorphisms, we derive bi-Lipschitz bounds for convex targets and for pairs of domains with Dini-smooth boundaries under the corresponding source regularity assumptions.

papers.title: Convergence analysis of generalized modified splitting methods using multi-index series
papers.abstract: We consider splitting methods for partial differential equations involving unbounded operators. For non-time-reversible dynamics, such as dissipative systems, negative splitting coefficients are generally not admissible because they require stepping backward in time, leading to an order barrier when all coefficients are required to be positive. We introduce generalized modified splitting methods that overcome this algebraic order barrier while retaining nonnegative splitting coefficients. To analyze their convergence, we develop a decorated multi-index series formalism and establish a substitution law that provides a systematic framework for deriving order conditions. This law also yields an order-raising procedure based on canceling the leading error through a modification of a single stage. We also derive an explicit composition law for extended multi-index series allowing the composition of methods with independently scaled time steps common in composition and processed methods. We illustrate the construction with two sixth-order methods that use different sets of commutator corrections. Python scripts automate the computation and verification of order conditions and the construction of the methods. Finally, we discuss connections with word series, Lie-Butcher series, and multi-index Butcher series.

papers.title: Integrals of some compound processes
papers.abstract: By means of the theory of compound (non-homogeneous) Poisson processes we define a general framework which includes most of the generalizations of the Poisson processes, both in the Skellam sense and in the space-fractional sense. We prove that Bernstein subordination is the only time change that leads to a compound Poisson process. We also consider the case of subordination with inverse Bernstein subordinators. Then, we focus on the integrals of compound processes. We give an explicit representation of the fractional integral of a compound Poisson process, showing that for fixed $t$ it is distributed as a compound Poisson random variable. We then extend this result to more general integral forms. Furthermore, we obtain some limit results, explicit forms of the iterated integrals and their governing equation. Finally, we study the integral of compound renewal processes in the Fourier-Laplace domain.

papers.title: Rigid motion invariant valuations on polytopes
papers.abstract: We show that any measurable, translation and $\mathrm{SO}(n)$-invariant valuation on polytopes in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a linear combination of the intrinsic volumes, which extends Hadwiger's classical characterization of rigid motion invariant continuous valuations on convex bodies. This result is based on a novel regularity result for translation invariant, measurable, $1$-homogeneous, and simple valuations. As a consequence, we obtain a similar characterization of the Steiner point map on polytopes.

papers.title: Quantitative Gibbs Transfer in Fiber-Contracting Extensions:\ Thermodynamic Formalism, Livšic Theory, and Sharp Logarithmic Distortion
papers.abstract: We study the transfer of Gibbs estimates between a compact dynamical system and a factor with uniformly contracting fibers. A cohomological identity relates the orbit sums; the remaining issue is the comparison of Bowen-ball masses. Subexponential comparison errors give directional weak Gibbs transfer, while bounded errors preserve strong estimates. We also establish a blockwise sequential version along prescribed Gibbs-time sequences, with errors measured against the full block length. Geometric and conditional-mass hypotheses provide practical criteria for these comparisons. A stationary renewal model shows that the distinction between bounded and subexponential comparison is essential. Its invariant lift to a contracting Cantor-fiber extension is not supported on a measurable graph, and the optimal uniform forward logarithmic error is $\log n+O(1)$. This remains true under fixed changes of the base radius. The reverse comparison, along a specified section, has bounded error. We also give an example in which pointwise subexponential bounds cannot be made uniform. For context, projection gives an affine bijection of invariant probability measures and preserves entropy. When the potentials are cohomologous, invariant averages and pressure agree, as do minimizing measures and equilibrium states in the finite-pressure regime. For Hölder potentials, a continuous section yields a stable-direction reduction, with Hölder regularity under additional assumptions. Subactions and Livšic solutions can then be lifted whenever the corresponding quotient hypotheses hold.
papers.comments: Title changed to "Quantitative Gibbs Transfer in Fiber-Contracting Extensions: Thermodynamic Formalism, Livšic Theory, and Sharp Logarithmic Distortion". Substantially revised and expanded version, with stronger Gibbs transfer theorems, sharp logarithmic distortion estimates, new examples, improved proofs, and updated references

papers.title: Counterexamples to Peskine-Szpiro's conjectures on modules of finite projective dimension
papers.abstract: We give counterexamples to the remaining homological conjectures of Peskine-Szpiro concerning modules of finite projective dimension over Noetherian local rings. Specifically, we show that the dimension inequality, the strong intersection conjecture, and the grade conjecture are all false in general.

papers.title: On the exact discretization of the $L_2$-norm in spaces generated by Rademacher functions and their $p$-adic analogues
papers.abstract: Sufficient conditions for the exact discretization of the $L_2$-norm in the space spanned by generalized Rademacher functions are proved. It is shown that the sufficient number of nodes for discretization with the minimal number of nodes is equal to $N$ or $N+1$ and depends on the dimension $N$. The conjecture of F.~Dai, A.~Prymak, V.~N.~Temlyakov, and S.~Yu.~Tikhonov on the positivity of weights in the exact discretization of the $L_2$-norm with a minimal number of points considered. It was investigated in which cases it holds and in which it fails for the spaces spanned by the $N$ generalized Rademacher functions with base $p$, and how the validity of the conjecture in this case depends on the parameters $p$ and $N$. The connection with generalized Hadamard matrices, the Hadamard's conjecture and Seberry's conjecture is demonstrated.

papers.title: Learning Informative Prior with Infinite-Dimensional Continuous Normalizing Flow for Bayesian Inverse Problem
papers.abstract: Infinite-dimensional Bayesian inference methods, as a core class of methodologies for solving inverse problems of partial differential equations, have been widely applied across numerous scientific fields. A critical obstacle to constructing effective Bayesian inversion methods is how to construct an informative prior measure, particularly in the infinite-dimensional setting. Based on an infinite-dimensionally well-defined neural ordinary differential equation, we establish a general learning framework for infinite-dimensional nonlinear transformations, which can be incorporated into two practical Bayesian prior-learning paradigms corresponding to the direct and indirect data scenarios. A key ingredient of this framework is an equivalence between non-Gaussian and Gaussian measures, which is highly nontrivial: nonlinear transformations with genuinely infinite-dimensional range are involved, and several new limiting mechanisms have to be clarified. The developed framework is applied to three representative inverse problems -- simple source inversion, inverse obstacle scattering, and inverse heat conduction. All three examples substantiate the effectiveness of the proposed methods and, at the same time, demonstrate their broad applicability.

papers.title: Lonely Runner Relations
papers.abstract: We study the \emph{Lonely Runner Conjecture} (LRC), conceived by Jörg M.~Wills in the 1960's: Given positive integers $n_1, n_2, \dots, n_k$, there exists a positive real number $t$ such that for all $1 \le j \le k$ the distance of $t \, n_j$ to the nearest integer is at least $\frac{ 1 }{ k+1 }$. We prove that for any counterexample or tight instance $\mathbf{n}$ of LRC, $\mathbf{m} \cdot \mathbf{n} = 0$ for some $\mathbf{m} \in \mathbb{Z}^k$ with $0 < \| \mathbf{m} \|_1 \le \min(2k+3, \ \frac{ k+1 }{ k-1 } \mathrm{flt}(k))$ where $\mathrm{flt}(k)$ denotes Khinchin's (1948) \emph{flatness constant} limiting the lattice width of a $k$-dimensional convex body without interior integer points. In other words, potential counterexamples to LRC lie on a finite set of hyperplanes in the parameter space. Our proofs use Fourier analysis and a geometric reformulation of LRC, and our results generalize to the situation of shifted lonely runners of varying measures of loneliness. Our results imply and generalize a theorem of Czerwiński (2012) that when we choose $\mathbf{n}$ at random then, with probability tending to 1, the measure of loneliness $\frac{ 1 }{ k+1 }$ can be replaced by $\frac 1 2 - ε$. We also show that the lattice width of the polyhedra appearing in conjunction with LRC grows linearly with the dimension.

papers.title: Global mild solutions and the semiclassical limit for the Fermi--Dirac BGK model
papers.abstract: We prove global existence of mild solutions to the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi--Dirac BGK equation for arbitrary-size Pauli-admissible initial data with finite mass and kinetic energy, allowing both vacuum and locally saturated zero-temperature states. The construction relies on a moment-compatible regularization of the local equilibrium that preserves the Pauli bound and uniform moment control while remaining consistent up to the saturation boundary. The solutions satisfy mass, momentum, and energy conservation and, under an additional finite spatial second-moment assumption, an entropy-gap H-theorem on the full Pauli interval. Under uniform moment and entropy bounds, we further prove that, after extraction of a subsequence, quantum mild solutions converge strongly in phase space, uniformly on bounded time intervals, to a mild solution of the classical BGK equation.
papers.comments: We have fixed typos, handled some minor errors, clarified some parts of the presentation, and included some recent references

papers.title: Power-saving density bounds for $K$-point configurations in $\mathbb{Z}^d$
papers.abstract: Let $d,K,N\in \mathbb{N}$ with $K\geq 3$ and $d\geq 4K+4$. Let $Δ\subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ be the vertex set of a nondegenerate $(K-1)$-simplex, and let $A\subseteq[N]^d$ contain no nontrivial similar copy of $Δ$. We prove that \[ |A|\ll_{Δ,d} N^{d-c_{Δ,d}}, \] improving upon a polylogarithmic bound due to Magyar. We combine an induction-on-scale argument with the circle method, and we introduce a ``cut operator'' method to decouple the weighted exponential sum over the system of quadratic forms describing the simplex. Our proof combines ideas from graph theory, functional analysis, and the geometry of numbers. In the process, we apply Finner's fractional form of Hölder's inequality, the analytic large sieve, and Kim's mean value formula for primitive lattice flags.
papers.comments: 39 pages. Significantly strengthened the main theorem by replacing the density increment with induction on scale. Streamlined exposition and expanded introduction with ideas for further directions

papers.title: Every integer greater than 24 is the sum of a prime and a non-square-free integer
papers.abstract: Lee and O'Clarey proved that every odd integer $n>24$ can be written as the sum of a prime and a positive integer that is not square-free. Under the generalised Riemann hypothesis, they established the same conclusion for every integer $n>24$. We prove this result unconditionally, confirming their stated expectation. The proof combines an elementary congruence argument, finite computation, and explicit estimates for primes in arithmetic progressions.
papers.comments: 8 pages. Substantial revision: the partial result in v1 has been extended to a complete unconditional proof. Title changed to reflect the stronger result

papers.title: Contact Large Deviations of Stochastic Vector Bundles
papers.abstract: A dissipative system distributes over its state space, and its rare events are measured on an exponential scale by a rate function. This paper shows that one contact form carries both. On the bundle of jets of probability densities over the state space, the constraint function of the contact potential is a first integral of the characteristic field, so the action is affine in the elapsed time along each characteristic and the contact probability measure of a Lagrangian section has that action as its exponent at every finite time, with no path integral, no variational problem over curves and no coercivity hypothesis. The rate function is the deficit of the action below its supremum, and is therefore a transported conserved quantity rather than the value of a limit; its amplitude is invariant and its non-degeneracy is decided by the initial section alone. Large deviations form the concentration regime of this finite-time structure and require one condition, the smooth convergence of the endpoint map of the characteristic flow to a diffeomorphism. The drift and the fluctuation tensor are the first two coefficients of the same potential, the second confined to the iso-density surfaces by the degeneracy condition, so the fluctuation is constrained by the invariant density rather than chosen beside the drift. The entropy production is an observable of the same measure, and a fibre involution yields a Gallavotti--Cohen-type duality between the forward and the reversed ensembles under a separation condition on the tilted action.

papers.title: Binary Minor Certificates for the $\mathcal A(1)$-hit problem of $MO(2)$
papers.abstract: Let $M=\widetilde H^*(MO(2);\mathbb F_2)$ and let $\mathcal A(1)$ be the subalgebra of the mod $2$ Steenrod algebra generated by $\operatorname{Sq}^1$ and $\operatorname{Sq}^2$. In this work, we determine the quotient $\mathbb F_2\otimes_{\mathcal A(1)}M$ in every internal degree $h\geq0$, where internal degree $h$ corresponds to cohomological degree $h+2$. To overcome the limitations of finite experimental extrapolation, our proof is strictly certifying: in each degree, we exhibit a determinant-one minor of the binary hit matrix and a complementary family of linear dual functionals annihilating every hit column, mathematically guaranteeing the exact rank for all degrees. This rigorously establishes the monomial generating families and module decomposition proposed in Shih's 2012 report. Furthermore, we derive a closed binomial formula for every Steenrod square from the length-two symmetric-polynomial model, correct a boundary omission in the $\mathcal A(0)$ calculation, compute the exact Hilbert series of the $\mathcal A(1)$-cohit, and prove an intrinsic direct-sum decomposition of $M$ into two stable $\mathcal A(1)$-submodules.

papers.title: Velocity Averaging for the Wigner Equation with Electromagnetic Fields
papers.abstract: We discuss the application of $L^2$-based velocity averaging to the Wigner kinetic equation governing the quantum evolution of the Wigner transform of a density operator of a particle subjected to an external electromagnetic field. This extends the $L^2$-based averaging lemma from [F. Golse, J. Möller: Commun. Math. Sci. (2026)] to electromagnetic fields. We make use of the magnetic or gauge-invariant Wigner transform due to Stratonovich [Sov. Phys. Dokl., 1:414-418, 1956] which differs from the usual definition by a phase factor involving the circulation of the magnetic vector potential along a line segment. The magnetic Wigner transform obeys the Wigner equation in the generalized phase space variables $(x,v=ξ-A(t,x))$, which is a more natural setting for the application of velocity averaging. Since the magnetic Wigner equation contains a first order derivative in the spatial variable, we obtain compactness in $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ but no gain in regularity.

papers.title: Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank I: Amata-Crupi monomial modules, Kozlov polytopes, and r-vectors of simplicial complexes
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be the exterior algebra on $n$ generators over a field, and let $F$ be a graded free $E$-module with $r$ generators, of degrees $d_1 \le \dots \le d_r$. We determine the convex hull of the set of Hilbert functions of the quotients $F/M$, where $M$ runs over the monomial submodules of Amata and Crupi. The hull is the Minkowski sum of $r$ shifted copies of one and the same simplex: the Kozlov simplex, which Kozlov proved in 1997 to be the convex hull of the $f$-vectors of simplicial complexes on $n$ vertices. For $r=1$ the statement is Kozlov's theorem, so this is a rank-$r$ generalization of it. We give a self-contained proof, including a proof of Kozlov's theorem from the local Lubell-Yamamoto-Meshalkin inequality, which is in essence Kozlov's own second proof, and the facet description of the Kozlov simplex that this proof contains. Along the way we isolate the class of submodules for which the argument works, the ideal-direct-sum modules, and show by example that the Hilbert function of a graded submodule outside that class need not be a shifted sum of $f$-vectors at all. The combinatorial content is stated separately, in language that uses no algebra, as a result on $r$-vectors of simplicial complexes and their $ff$-vectors. Finally we determine the vertices of the Minkowski sum at rank two: which sums of vertices of the summands survive as vertices. The facet descriptions at rank two, conjectured in the first version of this paper, and the vertex and facet descriptions at every rank are proved in Part IV of this series.
papers.comments: 53 pages. v2: facets of the Kozlov simplex attributed to Kozlov's second proof; the two rank-two facet conjectures are now theorems, proved in Part IV; Section 10 rewritten; numbering unchanged. Lean 4 formalization and code: https://github.com/JaTaSn/exterior-convex, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24288404; ancillary files with v1

papers.title: Universal existence and generic uniqueness for quadratic BSDE systems in a two-player stochastic differential game
papers.abstract: We study two-dimensional quadratic backward stochastic differential equations in the augmented natural filtration of a one-dimensional Brownian motion. The generator has components $q_{θ,i}(z)=z_i(z_1+z_2)-α_i z_i^2/2$, $i=1,2$, where $θ=(α_1,α_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2$. In the associated stochastic differential game, two players choose efforts $u_1,u_2$, the common state has drift $u_1+u_2$, and player $i$ pays $u_i^2/2$ per unit time and has risk sensitivity $α_i-1$. For every bounded terminal payoff vector $ξ$, which may depend on the entire state path, $(Y,Z)\mapsto Z$ is a bijection from solutions in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$ to Nash equilibria in BMO controls. Whether the risk-neutral system ($α_1=α_2=1$) is well posed for every such $ξ$ was left open in [Jackson (2023), Section 6.4]. For $α_1α_2\ne0$ with $α_1^{-1}+α_2^{-1}=1$, existence and uniqueness in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$ for every bounded $ξ$ were established in [Fan, Hu and Tang (2025), Corollary 2.25]. We prove that every bounded $ξ$ admits a solution in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$ for every $θ\in\mathbb{R}^2$. The solution is unique for every bounded $ξ$ if $(α_1-1)(α_2-1)=1$, but for every $θ$ with $(α_1-1)(α_2-1)\ne1$, we construct a bounded $ξ$ admitting at least two distinct solutions in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$. Nevertheless, for each $θ\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $M>0$, uniqueness holds on a dense $G_δ$ subset of the space of $[-M,M]^2$-valued terminal conditions equipped with the topology of convergence in probability. Moreover, if $ξ_n$ in this space converges in probability to a point $ξ$ of this subset, every choice of solutions for $ξ_n$ converges to the unique solution for $ξ$ in $\mathcal{S}^p\times\mathcal{H}^p$ for every $1\le p<\infty$.
papers.comments: 60 pages. This version proves existence for every bounded terminal condition, characterizes universal uniqueness for all real parameter pairs, and gives the corresponding results for Nash equilibria

papers.title: Non-vanishing of the structure-sheaf cohomology of affine henselian schemes and henselian affinoids
papers.abstract: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair such that $A$ is a domain of characteristic zero and $I\ne0$. We prove that any flat affine henselian scheme of finite presentation over $(A,I)$ has nonzero first structure-sheaf cohomology whenever one of its fibers over a point in $V(I)$ has positive dimension. This in particular gives a negative answer to the question by Devadas in the mixed-characteristic case. As an application, we also prove that the first structure-sheaf cohomology does not vanish for henselian affinoids of positive dimensions.
papers.comments: 15 pages. v2 included the detailed records of our conversations with the AI tools used in this work are publicly available at \url{https://github.com/utaka233/affine_henselian_schemes_20260925/}

papers.title: The word problem in verbal products of groups
papers.abstract: We prove that nilpotent and metabelian products of groups with decidable word problem have decidable word problem. In contrast, we exhibit families of groups with decidable word problem for which their solvable product has undecidable word problem. In doing so, we exhibit hyperbolic groups with undecidable membership problem in their derived subgroups.
papers.comments: 8 pages. Final version. It incorporates the referee's comments and suggestions. To appear in Groups, Geometry, and Dynamics

papers.title: An adaptive $L_2$-type test for high-dimensional white noise
papers.abstract: We propose a new $L_2$-type test for white noise which allows the dimension $p$ of the time series to either (i) be a fixed constant, or (ii) diverge with the sample size $n$. The proposed test statistic exhibits an interesting phase transition, following two different regimes of behavior: $p$ is fixed, and $p\rightarrow\infty$. Because identification of the operable regime is difficult, if not impossible in practice, we devise a novel adaptive bootstrap method to construct a unified testing procedure across different phases. Numerical experiments confirm the good finite sample performance of the proposed adaptive $L_2$-type test in comparison to the existing methods in the literature. The proposed testing procedure has been implemented in R package HDTSA.

papers.title: Log-concavity and Approximate Counting for Totally Unimodular Polytopes
papers.abstract: We present a new lower bound on the number of lattice points of all totally unimodular polytopes, generalizing previous lower bounds on contingency tables, integer flows, and beyond. Our bound is based on the Gurvits capacity convex optimization problem, and thus our result implies an efficient deterministic algorithm for approximate counting of the lattice points up to an explicit exponential factor. We achieve our bounds by showing that the associated generating polynomials fit into a new general class of log-concave polynomials called VLC ("variable-wise log-concavity''). This also implies a conjecture of Ferroni and Higashitani on the evaluations of the Ehrhart polynomials of unimodular polytopes. The essential ingredient for these results is the resolution of Barvinok's log-concavity conjecture for contingency tables on lines, which was proven using ChatGPT 6 Astra. We conjecture a generalization of Barvinok's conjecture, which we believe will lead to stronger and more general bounds.

papers.title: Non-Hermitian Yang--Mills Connections with Vanishing Chern Classes
papers.abstract: We construct non-flat non-Hermitian Yang--Mills connections with vanishing Chern classes whose induced and conjugate-dual holomorphic bundles are both stable, giving a negative answer to Kaledin and Verbitsky's flatness question even under these stability assumptions. We also give negative answers to their questions about the étaleness and bijectivity of the harmonic-class map. The examples are explicit connections on smoothly trivial rank-two bundles over projective Kähler surfaces and admit explicit positive harmonic metrics. For the family of fixed stable bundles studied here, the harmonic-class map is surjective. Every fibre contains exactly one flat point, but some fibres also contain positive-dimensional families of non-flat connections. The entire flat locus is a smooth component mapped biholomorphically onto the target. For a range of parameters, we determine the complete reduced analytic germ at a distinguished nonunitary flat point. It has two smooth branches of different dimensions whose intersection contains two-sided stable points arbitrarily close to that point. Finally, a single fibre of the pair of holomorphic projections contains infinitely many flat classes and an embedded copy of $\CC^*$ with exactly two flat members. Thus the two holomorphic isomorphism classes together do not determine flatness.

papers.title: A question of Ulam and a theorem of de Rham
papers.abstract: We generalize de Rham's decomposition theorem to proper metric spaces: every proper metric space has a unique decomposition as the product of a Euclidean space and a finite or countable pointed $\ell^2$-product of nontrivial irreducible non-Euclidean factors. A slightly weaker unique decomposition statement is verified for general complete metric spaces. We use this to resolve a question of Ulam on the uniqueness of square roots of complete metric spaces.
papers.comments: Added a resolution of Ulam's question for complete metric spaces

papers.title: Transcending Algebraic Geometry
papers.abstract: We give an exposition of some of the ideas leading up to Jacob Tsimerman's groundbreaking work developing the theory of o-minimal definability in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.

papers.title: A Pogorelov-type estimate for the real twisted Monge-Ampère equation
papers.abstract: We establish a Pogorelov type interior $C^2$ estimate for the real twisted Monge-Ampere equation without assuming uniform ellipticity. This equation is fully nonlinear and elliptic, but is neither concave nor a function of the eigenvalues of the Hessian, so the standard techniques for interior second-derivative estimates do not directly apply. Building on the partial Legendre transform formulation of Streets and Warren, we derive a differential identity for the associated positive-definite matrix $W(D^2u)$ and use some linear algebra to control the third-order terms arising in the maximum principle argument. As an application, we prove a Liouville theorem for entire split convex solutions with quadratic growth, extending the rigidity theorem of Streets and Warren by replacing their uniform ellipticity hypothesis with suitable quadratic growth assumptions.
papers.comments: 27 pages. Revised title. Improved arguments to take place purely in direct coordinates

papers.title: Central algebraic cohomology of Galois gerbes and its abelianization
papers.abstract: We study central algebraic cohomology and its abelianization for Galois gerbes over local fields of characteristic zero and over number fields. The coefficients consist of a connected reductive group and a central subgroup that need not be finite or connected. We construct a canonical abelian group structure on abelian central cohomology. When the gerbe admits a morphism from Kaletha's rigid gerbe, we obtain a fiber product formula for this group in terms of rigid cohomology and homomorphisms from the band to the central subgroup. Over number fields, abelianization and localization at the real places recover the full central cohomology set. We obtain explicit formulas for Kottwitz's local and global gerbes and for Fargues's extended Kottwitz gerbe.
papers.comments: 45 pages. Version 2 constructs a canonical abelian group structure on abelian central cohomology and add explicit formulas for Fargues's extended Kottwitz gerbe

papers.title: The monatomic limit of polyatomic gases: the Dirac prescription and an application to a new hierarchy of moments
papers.abstract: In the kinetic theory of a polytropic gas, internal molecular modes are described by a power-law density of internal states, making the monatomic limit singular. We show that the normalized limit $a\to-1^+$ is equivalent to replacing integration over internal energy by a Dirac mass at zero energy, and derive the first-order correction. We apply this prescription to the classical full-energy moment hierarchy arising from the non-relativistic limit of the relativistic hierarchy of Arima, Carrisi, Pennisi and Ruggeri. For every finite truncation order, we establish the independent and exhaustive monatomic trace identities and derive the number of surviving fields. In particular, the known reduction from polyatomic ET15 to Kremer's monatomic ET14 is recovered. We also prove that the limiting spectrum of the unreduced polyatomic characteristic pencil splits into the spectrum of the reduced monatomic system and a lower-order polyatomic spectrum with a shifted internal-energy parameter. Equilibrium characteristic velocities are obtained using the linearized maximum-entropy prescription, without assuming a nonlinear closure away from equilibrium. We show that, at fixed truncation order, the largest characteristic velocity is non-increasing with the number of molecular degrees of freedom and attains its maximum at the monatomic endpoint. Finally, the symmetric-hyperbolic principal-subsystem argument yields the previously known Boillat--Ruggeri lower bound for the new hierarchy, implying unbounded growth of the maximum characteristic velocity with truncation order.
papers.comments: 36 pages, 1 figure. Substantially revised and extended version with a new title, including the monatomic reduction of the full-energy moment hierarchy and a systematic analysis of equilibrium characteristic velocities

papers.title: Seed thresholds and degree variance in heterogeneous bootstrap percolation with growing degrees
papers.abstract: We study bootstrap percolation with independent vertex thresholds taking values one and two, with threshold-one probability $(1-c/d)/d$ for fixed $c>0$. The seed set is chosen uniformly among sets of a prescribed deterministic size, independently of the graph and thresholds. We prove threshold statements at fixed relative margins. For uniform simple graphs with prescribed nonnegative integer degrees of even sum and exact mean $d$, assume $\max_i|d_i-d|\le C\sqrt d$ and $c+1-v_n\geκ>0$, where $v_n=\operatorname{Var}(D)/d$ and $C,κ$ are fixed. When $d\to\infty$ and $d=o(n^{1/7})$, the leading seed scale is $n(c+1-v_n)^2/(2d^4)$, without requiring a limit of $v_n$. At fixed relative margins below and above this scale, the final active set has size $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$, respectively, with high probability. For regular graphs, the supercritical conclusion strengthens to full activation. For $G(n,d/n)$, the same $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$ conclusions hold when $d\to\infty$ and $d^5/n\to0$, with seed scale $nc^2/(2d^4)$. Thus regular and independent-edge graphs have different coefficients at the same asymptotic mean degree. Local exploration estimates yield explicit inactive remainders and survive conditioning on simplicity in the prescribed model. We also quantify the precision obstruction to static inclusion transfer and compute deterministic response-barrier corrections, without identifying a shrinking random critical window. A separate appendix gives the corresponding fixed-margin terminal bounds for iid thresholds of fixed bounded support, with unchanged threshold-one probability and threshold-two mass bounded away from zero.
papers.comments: 31 pages. In v3, Appendix C extends the fixed-margin terminal bounds to iid thresholds of fixed bounded support

papers.title: Plunge bounds for Fourier concentration operators: geometry, smoothing, and wave packets
papers.abstract: We prove a single-logarithm bound for the eigenvalues in the plunge region of Fourier concentration operators, removing the extra logarithmic factor in the Kulikov--Dam Larsen bound for two general admissible sets throughout each fixed exponential window. For bounded spatial and frequency sets $A,B\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of positive measure with finite upper codimension-one Minkowski boundary content, the number $Λ_\varepsilon(cA,B)$ of eigenvalues in $(\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon)$ satisfies $Λ_\varepsilon(cA,B)\le C(d,A,B,β)c^{d-1}D(1+\log_+(c/D))$, where $D=\log(1/(\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)))$, for every fixed $β>0$, $c\ge2$, $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, and $D\leβc$, with $\log_+t=\max(0,\log t)$. The argument uses positive band-limited smoothing and requires no symmetry, convexity, or connectedness. In dimension two, the corresponding exponential-window estimate has a constant uniform in the window parameter. We also determine the optimal coordinate-Lipschitz constant $d-1$ for recursive decompositions of balls and standard simplices in every dimension, and obtain box-frequency estimates with explicit geometric constants. For $C^1$ convex bodies in three dimensions, the optimal infimum of recursive coordinate slopes is $2$. Uniform real-order Bessel estimates give independent disk and ball bounds at every spectral threshold, including an explicit deep-tail term. For smooth strictly convex planar frequency bodies with positive curvature, we prove correlation estimates for aligned Gaussian packets at arbitrary relative scales and quantitative lower bounds on the cost of estimating spatial blocks separately. Together these results connect the global spectral bound with sharp geometric constructions and the cancellation retained by grouping boundary interactions.
papers.comments: Withdrawn by the author; the results will be incorporated into a forthcoming joint work

papers.title: An explicit tame factorization of the four-variable Anick automorphism
papers.abstract: Let $δ=xz-yt$. We give an explicit tame factorization of the Anick automorphism $$ f=(x+δt,y+δz,z,t) $$ of $F[x,y,z,t]$. After a linear change of coordinates, the factorization consists of sixteen elementary automorphisms, all fixing $z$. The proof uses a commutator construction with variables already present in the algebra. A complete list of the elementary factors is included in Section 5. The explicit polynomial factorization identities are defined over $Z[1/2]$; no conclusion in characteristic $2$ is asserted. We also prove that the Freudenburg--Moser-Jauslin involution $$ τ(a,b,x,y)= \bigl(b,a,-b^3x+(1+ab+a^2b^2)y,(1-ab)x+a^3y\bigr). $$ of $F[a,b,x,y]$ is tame over every field of characteristic different from $2$ and $3$, and list an explicit factorization in Appendix.

papers.title: Wyner's Common Information and the Common Entropy are NP-Hard to Compute
papers.abstract: Wyner's common information $J(P_{XY})$ and the common entropy $G(P_{XY})$ of a pair of finite random variables $(X,Y)$ with joint distribution $P_{XY}$ minimize, respectively, the mutual information $I(X,Y;W)$ and the entropy $H(W)$ over all auxiliary random variables $W$ that make $X$ and $Y$ conditionally independent. We prove that both quantities are NP-hard to compute, by polynomial-time reductions from the Maximum Edge Biclique problem. Moreover, unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, no polynomial-time algorithm can approximate $J(P_{XY})$ within an additive error $1/(8N^2)$, or $G(P_{XY})$ within an additive error $1/(2N)$, where $N$ is the number of positive entries of $P_{XY}$.
papers.comments: Updated version of the manuscript. Submitted for publication

papers.title: Cone Restriction Estimates under Half-Scale Dimensional Conditions
papers.abstract: We prove cone restriction estimates under half-scale dimensional conditions. Building on the framework of Du--Li--Wang--Zhang, we incorporate the broad restriction estimate of Ou--Wang and a localized multilinear estimate obtained through cyclic bilinear pairing and multilinear Kakeya bounds for local packet $L^2$-norm. The zero-dimensional case yields a large-value estimate on $R^{1/2}$-cubes. For certain ambient and weight dimensions, our estimates are sharp in suitable ranges of $p$, up to an $R^\varepsilon$ loss.

papers.title: Covering Radius and Deep Holes of Hyperderivative Reed-Solomon Codes under the NRT Metric
papers.abstract: The deep hole problem is a fundamental problem in coding theory, and it has many important applications in code constructions and cryptography. The deep hole problem of Reed-Solomon codes has gained a lot of attention. Hyperderivative Reed-Solomon (HRS) codes under the Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman (NRT) metric generalize Reed-Solomon codes under the Hamming metric. We study the covering radius and deep holes of HRS codes in the NRT metric. We prove that the NRT covering radius of $\mathrm{HRS}_k(α,V)$ is $sr-k$ and characterize its NRT deep holes via an MDS-extension criterion and a polynomial-remainder criterion. The latter yields an enumeration formula in terms of the characteristic polynomial of an associated hyperplane arrangement. We also construct three families of NRT deep holes and derive exact enumeration formulas in several special cases, including $r \in \{1,2\}$ and $k \in \{1,2,sr-1,sr-2,sr-3\}$. For full-length evaluation sets and $s \geq 2$, we completely describe the deep holes for $2 \leq k \leq sq-1$ whenever $q$ is odd or $k \geq 3$. When $k \geq s$, the deep holes are precisely the evaluations of polynomials of degree $k$. For $k<s$, we give an explicit description.

papers.title: Ending currents of hyperbolic group actions
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of ending currents for properly discontinuous isometric actions of hyperbolic groups on Gromov hyperbolic spaces, generalizing Thurston's ending laminations. Several natural generalizations are considered, which agree in the 3-dimensional hyperbolic setting but are otherwise distinct. We illustrate these invariants and their differences by several examples, including closed surface group actions on hyperbolic group extensions arising from Teichmüller theory and a geometrically finite action of a closed surface group on $\mathbb{H}^4$ with a single cusp that corresponds to a non-simple curve on the surface. We also discuss the conditions under which ending currents characterize geometrically finite actions, obtaining several equivalent conditions and some surprises, illustrated by an example of a geometrically infinite action whose ending currents are all supported on a single orbit of peripheral subgroups.

papers.title: Safety stock calculation with heteroscedastic, autocorrelated and heavy-tailed forecast errors, an adaptive parametric method.e
papers.abstract: This study develops and validates an adaptive parametric method for sizing safety stock when forecast errors are autocorrelated, heteroscedastic, asymmetric, and heavy-tailed. Using four years of weekly forecasts from a fast-moving consumer goods company, the analysis identifies substantial positive autocorrelation, departures from normality, systematic forecast optimism, and heterogeneous relationships between forecast volume and error variance. The proposed method integrates several corrections into a modular, sequential safety-stock architecture. It constructs cumulative forecast errors over the operational action period, selects an SKU-specific parametric distribution, and determines a baseline protection point using an expected-shortage condition consistent with the target beta fill rate. A forecast-scaled module adjusts dispersion when error variance depends on forecast volume, while a Cycle-End Exposure safeguard limits within-cycle shortage risk when large replenishment lots increase exposure. Performance is evaluated through discrete-event simulation against the company's current method. The proposed method reduces average inventory by 9.9% and maximum inventory by 19.5%, with no statistically significant deterioration in beta fill rate or average stockout duration. The proportion of weeks without stockouts declines slightly, without evidence of more persistent or operationally severe shortages. The heteroscedasticity module provides selective benefits, with greater service improvements as variance dependence intensifies. The resulting framework is interpretable, adapts to SKU-specific statistical profiles, links distributional features to safety-stock outcomes, and can be integrated into existing ERP environments.

papers.title: Scaled Companion Linearizations for Coefficientwise Backward Stability
papers.abstract: A backward stable eigensolver applied to a linearization of a matrix polynomial does not necessarily produce eigenpairs with small coefficientwise relative backward errors. Scaling the polynomial can help, but a single scaling may not provide coefficientwise backward stability across the entire spectrum, particularly when the eigenvalues have widely varying magnitudes. To address this difficulty, we use different scalings in different regions of the spectrum. We partition the nonzero complex plane into radial regions and, for each region, construct a scaled companion linearization with an eigenvector recovery rule.
