With known support and oracle state pairs, the asymptotic covariance approaches the Cramér--Rao bound as smoothing vanishes and is strictly smaller than that of any Gaussian quasi-likelihood estimator under an explicit non-Gaussianity condition; for unknown sparse support we characterize the boundary limit, and we quantify the topology bias caused by residual-score mismatch. Third, we couple score-driven graph updates with an approximately fully adapted generative particle filter and prove, for bounded residuals under explicit excitation and forgetting conditions, a mean-square closed-loop bound with a step-size-independent small-gain condition. Synthetic and real-data experiments confirm these gains under non-Gaussian forcing.

papers.title: A disproof of the van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk conjecture on the Davenport constant
papers.abstract: The Davenport constant $D(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence $S$ with terms from $G$ and with length $|S| \ge \ell$ has a nontrivial zero-sum subsequence. A long-standing conjecture, first proposed by van Emde Boas and Kruyswijk in 1969, states that $D(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1$ for all positive integers $n$ and $r$. We disprove this conjecture for every exponent $n=2k$ with $k\ge3$ odd. For each such $n$, we prove that $D(C_n^r)>r(n-1)+1$ for every $r\ge \frac{5n}{2}$. For rank $r=3$, we prove that the equality $D(C_n^3)=3n-2$ holds for all sufficiently large integers $n$.

papers.title: Formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a connected finite-type CW-complex with a map to the circle that is surjective on fundamental groups. If $X$ is formal, the algebraic monodromy of the associated infinite cyclic cover has no Jordan block of size greater than one at the eigenvalue 1, over the rationals; formality of the $d$-fold cyclic cover rules out such blocks at the $d$-th roots of unity. We study how formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy constrain each other. We call $X$ Alexander formal if there are no such blocks at any root of unity, rationally, nor at the eigenvalue 1 modulo any prime; this is a formality property of cochains, as DG modules over the cohomology of the circle. The complement of a central hyperplane arrangement, with its Milnor fibration, is Alexander formal exactly when the numbers of hyperplanes in its irreducible factors have no common divisor greater than 1. We also show that a CDGA graded by an abelian group, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, is formal if and only if it is formal as a graded CDGA. Hence the strong formality of Kohno and Pajitnov implies formality of every finite abelian cover of $X$, but not conversely. Modulo $p$, eigenvalues of $p$-power order collide with 1, producing Jordan blocks that strong formality allows; the two conditions are incomparable, and all four resulting classes contain arrangement complements.

papers.title: Multiple Positive Solutions of Minkowski-Curvature Neumann Problems with a Two-Step Indefinite Weight
papers.abstract: We study the multiplicity of positive solutions of the following Minkowski-curvature Neumann problem \[ \begin{aligned} \left(\frac{u'}{\sqrt{1-(u')^2}}\right)' +a(t)g(u)&=0,\quad t\in(0,T),\\ u'(0)=u'(T)&=0, \end{aligned} \] where $a$ is a two-step sign-changing weight with negative mean. We establish a multiplicity criterion for positive solutions, give a negative answer to the uniqueness question raised by Boscaggin, Feltrin and Zanolin, and prove the existence of infinitely many positive solutions for a fixed weight. The proofs are based on the shooting method and uniform asymptotic estimates.

papers.title: Combinatorial Dvoretzky Theory
papers.abstract: Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be an $n$-dimensional polytope such that $P \subset B_2^n$. Let $M^*(P)$ denote its mean width, and let $N$ be the number of facets (faces of dimension $n-1$) of $P$. We prove the following two bounds: (1) If $N \leq e^n$, then \[ M^*(P) \leq 1 - \frac{c}{\log^2(\frac{N}{n})}. \] (2) For arbitrary $N$, \[ M^*(P) \leq 1 - \frac{c}{n}N^{-\frac{2}{n-1}}. \] In both bounds, $c>0$ is an absolute constant.

papers.title: Local cohomology module with infinitely many associated primes over ramified regular local rings of the least possible dimensions
papers.abstract: In \cite{Ma} we have observed the example of local cohomology module with infinitely many associated primes over a 12 dimensional ramified regular local ring. In this paper we construct examples of local cohomology modules with infinitely many associated primes over ramified regular local rings of two different ring dimensions. The result of this paper is very much dependent on the result (\cite{SS}, Theorem 2.6).
papers.comments: Some error is detected in the proof. So I withdraw it. Sorry for the inconvenience

papers.title: Square-root cancellation in three hyperbolic counting problems via maximal estimates
papers.abstract: We study three counting problems for lattice orbits in hyperbolic space: counting orbit points within a prescribed distance of a fixed closed geodesic or a totally geodesic hyperplane, and counting orbit points above a prescribed height at a cusp. For almost every base point, we obtain error bounds of square-root size up to logarithmic factors. For the geodesic and hyperplane counts, these bounds match the conjectured exponents and improve earlier results due to Good and Laaksonen. For these two problems, we adapt the method of maximal estimates developed by Chatzakos and Dimakis for hyperbolic lattice counting, formulating it in both a discrete and a continuous framework. For the hyperplane problem, we also obtain an asymptotic formula for the spatial second moment of the error term, involving an almost periodic function. For the cusp problem, the square-root bound can be deduced from work of Yu, which incorporates Schmidt's dyadic maximal argument. We present a proof, together with an $Ω$-result supporting the optimality of the exponent $1/2$ for at least one cusp of any group that is not essentially cuspidal.

papers.title: Well-posedness and finite-time breakdown for Euler-alignment systems with diffusive chemotaxis
papers.abstract: We investigate a recent class of pressureless Euler systems arising in biological contexts, in which the velocity evolution is driven, besides the nonlocal alignment interaction, by the gradient of a concentration self-produced by the population. We first establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, in a class requiring no spatial derivative of the initial population density, together with a continuation criterion. We then derive sufficient conditions on the initial data for finite-time breakdown in the multidimensional setting, with an explicit upper bound for the maximal time of existence. Numerical simulations complement the analysis and illustrate the transition between regular and singular regimes, and the role of the chemotactic strength in the onset of blow-up.

papers.title: The standard filtration of Leavitt path algebras and topological full groups
papers.abstract: We consider several problems related to the growth of Leavitt path algebras with respect to the natural length filtration. We define the generating function of the series of dimensions of the successive quotients of this filtration and show that it is a rational function with poles which are reciprocal of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix, a fact which is related to recent results by Bock, Gil Canto, Martín Barquero, Martín González, Ruiz Campos and Sebandal on algebraic entropy of Leavitt path algebras. We also consider the filtration induced in the topological full group of the Renault-Deaconu groupoid of the defining graph and study the growth of the associated series. In the particular case of Thompson's group $V$, we find double exponential upper and lower bounds for this growth. We also prove related results for the group $F$ and for some submonoids.

papers.title: A proof of the weighted Böttcher-Wenzel inequality conjectured by Mayumi, Kimura, Ohno and Chruściński
papers.abstract: For a positive definite matrix $ω$ with two smallest eigenvalues $λ_1\leλ_2$ and the weighted Frobenius norm $\|X\|_ω^2=\mathrm{Tr}(X^*Xω)$, Mayumi, Kimura, Ohno and Chruściński conjectured that $\|[A,B]\|_ω^2\le\frac{λ_1+λ_2}{λ_1λ_2}\|A\|_ω^2\|B\|_ω^2$ for all complex matrices $A,B$. We prove this inequality for real and for complex matrices of every size, by a short computer-free argument, and we determine the cases of equality. In fact $\|XZY-YZX\|_2\le\|Z\|_{(2),2}\|X\|_2\|Y\|_2$ for all complex matrices of compatible sizes, where $\|Z\|_{(2),2}$ is the Ky Fan $(2),2$ norm (the $\ell^2$ norm of the two largest singular values), and the constant is attained unless $X$ and $Y$ are $1\times1$ matrices; the conjecture is the case $Z=ω^{-1/2}$. The best constant is the square of a unitarily invariant norm of $Z$, which is convex, so it suffices to treat weights whose $n-1$ largest eigenvalues coincide. For these, an inequality for one matrix and a pair of unit vectors, written in bases adapted to the pair of unit vectors, reduces the conjecture to the positive semidefiniteness of an explicit $4\times4$ Hermitian matrix depending on a $2\times2$ matrix $B$ in a convex set defined by two weighted operator-norm bounds, and an explicit determinant identity writes its determinant as a sum of products of factors that are visibly nonnegative; the phases of the entries of $B$ enter only through $|\det B|^2$, so the real case is literally a special case. As a second theorem we prove, for every weight, a strengthening of the conjecture that is equivalent to the inequality for one matrix and all pairs of unit vectors; its best constant is again a convex function of $ω^{-1/2}$, and the same argument applies. We also read the inequality as a sharp bound for inner derivations on the GNS space of a faithful state.
papers.comments: 30 pages, 1 table. v2: AI declaration reworded, one citation updated

papers.title: Tight Lipschitz Hardness for Solving Random Polynomial Equations
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of solving $n$ polynomial equations in $d$ real variables: $F_1({\boldsymbol x})=0, \ldots, F_n({\boldsymbol x})=0$, with unknowns ${\boldsymbol x}=(x_1, \ldots, x_d)$ satisfying the normalization constraint $\|{\boldsymbol x}\|=1$, when the polynomials are i.i.d. realization of a rotationally invariant Gaussian process. In previous work (Montanari, Subag, 2023), we developed an iterative algorithm that attempts to minimize the energy function $H({\boldsymbol x})=\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})\|^2/2$ (with ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})=(F_i({\boldsymbol x}):i\le n)$), using first and second order information (gradient and Hessian of $H$) at a sequence of query points ${\boldsymbol x}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol x}_k$. Here, we prove a lower bound on the minimum energy achieved by any algorithm that is Lipschitz continuous in the coefficients of the polynomials $F_i$. We prove that the lower bound matches the the energy achieved by the algorithm in (Montanari, Subag, 2023), hence characterizing the degree of accuracy to which the system of equations ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})={\boldsymbol 0}$ can be solved by Lipschitz algorithms. Our results imply that, for certain choices of the distribution of the polynomials $F_i$, solutions exist with high probability but Lipschitz algorithms fails to find near-solutions, even in a very weak sense. Namely, if ${\boldsymbol x}^{alg}$ is the output of a Lipschitz algorithm, then $\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x}^{alg})\|^2\ge \varepsilon {\mathbb E}[\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x}_0)\|^2]$ (for ${\boldsymbol x}_0$ a non-random point on the unit sphere) with high probability for some $\varepsilon>0$. The proof is based on techniques developed in the context of spin glass theory.

papers.title: Inverse problems for ZS operators and their isomorphisms, II
papers.abstract: We study isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators on the unit interval with generic boundary conditions. A unitary gauge transformation reduces these problems to the corresponding problems with basic boundary conditions, with an explicit shift of the spectral parameter. Using previous results for canonical boundary conditions and four-spectra data mapping we describe isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators. Moreover, we study other inverse problems including replacing mappings and canonical relations.

papers.title: A Proof of Blackburn's Conjecture on Non-Overlapping Codes
papers.abstract: A code is non-overlapping if no nonempty proper prefix of a codeword is a suffix of a codeword. Let $S_n(q)$ be the largest size of a non-overlapping code of length $n$ over an alphabet of size $q$. Levenshtein proved that $S_n(q)\le c_nq^n$, where $c_n=(1/n)\bigl((n-1)/n\bigr)^{n-1}$. The codes $I^{n-1}J$, where $I$ and $J$ partition the alphabet, attain this bound when $n$ divides $q$, and Blackburn conjectured that for every $n$ and all sufficiently large $q$, the best such code is a maximum non-overlapping code. We prove this conjecture. The proof uses generating functions for the nested partitions that describe maximal non-overlapping codes. We also show that only the codes $I^{n-1}J$ with $|I|=(n-1)q/n$ and their reversals meet Levenshtein's bound.

papers.title: Elliptic curves with torsion Z/5Z: exact rank four over Q(k) and rank at least five infinitely often
papers.abstract: We give two elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}(k)$ with torsion group $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ and rank exactly $4$, with four explicit independent points. The upper bounds come from reducing the relevant elliptic surfaces modulo suitable primes and are unconditional. They match the known lower bound for the generic rank with this torsion, due to Eroshkin, and are not isomorphic to Eroshkin's curve or to each other: their parametrising maps to $X_1(5)$ have degree $8$ instead of $12$, the constructions are dihedral rather than biquadratic, and their branch loci differ. In each case, two of the points come from a ``doubling'' step in the spirit of Jaswal. Adding one further condition to the second curve, coming from a quadratic twist over an intermediate conic, gives a fifth independent point over a genus-one curve of rank two. Hence there are infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ and rank at least $5$, improving the known bound $C(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z})\ge 4$ to $C(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z})\ge 5$.

papers.title: Computer-Aided Analysis of Gradient Descent under Generalized Smoothness
papers.abstract: Under classical assumptions, performance of first-order methods has been studied quite comprehensively with the developed theoretical apparatus of modern optimization. The development of the Performance Estimation Problems (PEP) framework led to even deeper understanding and allowed computer-assisted derivation of exact worst-case guarantees. Unfortunately, PEP is not directly applicable for systems that involve SDP-incompatible constraints. This includes a wide range of non-standard assumptions, some of them are highly relevant for practice such as generalized smoothness. In this paper proposes an approach of utilizing template solutions to derive guarantees in settings that do not admit an equivalent SDP formulation of exact worst-case performance problem. The approach is showcased by studying the performance of the gradient descent method for convex functions that also satisfy $(L_0,L_1)$-smoothness assumption. Despite the inherent conservatism of the approach, this paper improves and generalizes an existing convergence guarantee to showcase the approach.
papers.comments: This is the extended version of the paper Krivchenko, V. O. (2026). Computer-Aided Analysis of Gradient Descent under Generalized Smoothness. Doklady Mathematics, 530(1), 5-13. The extended version is much more detailed. It contains expanded discussion of the approach as well as descriptions of PEP experiments

papers.title: Strict hot spots and absence of interior critical points on simply connected planar Hölder domains
papers.abstract: Every nonzero real eigenfunction for the first positive Neumann eigenvalue on a bounded simply connected planar Hölder domain has no interior critical point. The Hölder condition is quasihyperbolic; equivalently, a Riemann map has derivative in $L^{2p}$ for some $p>1$. This includes Lipschitz domains and polygons with reentrant corners. Multiple eigenvalues and non-Jordan boundaries are allowed. The proof uses boundary primitives, a uniform multiplier estimate, and approximation of the whole limiting eigenspace. When this eigenspace is two-dimensional, every real basis gives global coordinates onto a domain star-shaped about the origin. A stream function proves injectivity and yields a Poisson formula for the boundary angular derivative. The conformal boundary map has a Lipschitz inverse and a rectifiable Jordan image; its boundary angle is a circle diffeomorphism with nonvanishing Hölder-continuous derivative. The image can be nonconvex even when the source is smooth and strictly convex.

papers.title: Rotational Chaos in the Driven Pendulum
papers.abstract: Building on recent developments in the topological theory of surface dynamics, we develop readily applicable criteria for computer-assisted proofs of the existence of rotational horseshoes and apply them to the Driven Pendulum. These tools also allow us to localize the resulting instability region, and to compute a lower bound for the length of their rotation sets. This, in turn, implies the existence of periodic points realizing a wide range of rational rotation numbers. The obtained results correspond to physically meaningful parameter values of the Driven Pendulum. The method also applies to periodically forced Hamiltonian systems whenever the stated conditions are satisfied.

papers.title: Interpolation of nonlocal Sobolev spaces for general gradients
papers.abstract: We study the interpolation structure of nonlocal Sobolev spaces associated with general radial gradients. For compactly supported kernels satisfying suitable regularity and two-sided growth assumptions of fractional order, we characterize the spaces $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $1<p<\infty$, by the Gustavsson--Peetre interpolation method between $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $W^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. The function parameter is determined, up to equivalence, by the behavior of the kernel near the origin. We also establish a complex interpolation formula between spaces associated with different kernels and integrability exponents, in which the interpolated kernel is their geometric mean. For the corresponding nonlocal Gagliardo spaces $W^{ρ,p}(\R^n)$, defined through an integral seminorm of first differences, we prove an identification with generalized Besov spaces and a real interpolation characterization involving the same function parameter. These results extend the classical relation between Bessel potential and Gagliardo spaces beyond power-type kernels, yielding continuous embeddings between the two families and their coincidence in the Hilbertian case. We further discuss logarithmic kernels and restriction spaces on Lipschitz domains, and obtain extension and compact embedding results for the Gagliardo spaces under weaker assumptions on the kernel.

papers.title: OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture: A harmonic analytic perspective
papers.abstract: This note presents OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture. It is written for harmonic analysts who may be new to quaternionic Monge--Ampère equations. We introduce the quaternionic Hessian and explain how the associated determinant equation leads to the critical annular estimate.

papers.title: Hyperconvexity of pseudoconvex domains with continuous boundaries
papers.abstract: This is a reading note on a disc formula proof of hyperconvexity of bounded pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb C^n$ with continuous boundaries.
papers.comments: Reading note of an AI proof. Second version: add a remark of our main theorem by Bo-Yong Chen in the Acknowledgements --- bounded pseudoconvex domain with Hölder continuous boundary has positive hyperconvexity index. Correct a typo for the definition of D in the proof of the main theorem

papers.title: Eigenvalues of doubly stochastic matrices in large orders
papers.abstract: For $1\le k\le N$, every point in the convex hull of the $k$th roots of unity is an eigenvalue of some doubly stochastic matrix of order $N$. Perfect and Mirsky asked whether any other eigenvalues occur. We prove that the union of these polygons is the whole region for every $N\ge450$. Our pencil-and-paper proof for $N\ge10^{30}$ starts with an eigenvector $v$ of Euclidean norm one. Place one unit of mass at each coordinate $v_j$. If $Av=zv$, row $i$ draws mass $A_{ij}$ from each mark $v_j$, so the mass it receives has centre $zv_i$. The column sums ensure that each mark supplies one unit in total. It follows that the sum of the row variances is $1-|z|^2$. Since the regular $N$-gon contains the disk of radius $\cos(π/N)$, an eigenvalue outside the polygons would force this sum below $\sin^2(π/N)$. We use this bound to compare permutations of the outer marks and to follow a randomly chosen mark through a quarter turn. To reach $450$, we count marks between concentric circles and verify a finite set of inequalities by computer. We also determine the regions in orders five and six by computer-assisted proofs. At order five the full region is obtained by adding to the polygons the segments from the origin to two conjugate arcs traced by roots of quartic polynomials. At order six the square, pentagon and hexagon give the whole region.
papers.comments: 58 pages, 8 figures, 12 references. Substantial revision with a new title. The present version proves the polygonal region in all orders $N\ge450$ and gives complete computer-assisted descriptions in orders five and six. Verification code and data are included as ancillary files

papers.title: Minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous and bounded
papers.abstract: We prove Ambro's conjecture stating that the minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous. As a consequence, minimal log discrepancies are bounded from above by the dimension of the variety, proving a conjecture of Shokurov.
papers.comments: Lemma 3.2 is false. The proof fails because $S_{m'}$ is only constructible and not an algebraic stack. I thank all the people that pointed out the mistake

papers.title: On $β=6$ Tracy-Widom distribution and the second Calogero-Painlevé system
papers.abstract: The Calogero-Painlevé systems were introduced in 2001 by K. Takasaki as a natural generalization of the classical Painlevé equations to the case of the several Painlevé ``particles'' coupled via the Calogero type interactions. In 2014, I. Rumanov discovered the remarkable fact that a particular case of the second Calogero-Painlevé II equation describes the Tracy-Widom distribution function for the general beta-ensembles with even values of the parameter beta. Most recently, in 2017 work of M. Bertola, M. Cafasso, and V. Rubtsov, it was proven that all Calogero-Painlevé systems are Lax integrable, and hence their solutions admit a Riemann-Hilbert representation. This important observation has opened the door to rigorous, based on the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method, asymptotic analysis of the Calogero-Painlevé equations. This in turn yields the possibility of rigorous evaluation of the asymptotic behavior of the Tracy-Widom distributions for the values of beta beyond the classical $β=1, 2, 4.$ In this work we shall start an asymptotic analysis of the Calogero-Painlevé system with a special focus on the Calogero-Painlevé system corresponding to $β= 6$ Tracy-Widom distribution function. The principle technical challenge is the implementation of the nonlinear steepest descent approach beyond the $2\times 2$ matrix dimension of the corresponding Riemann-Hilbert problem; in our case, it is $6\times 6$.
papers.comments: 60 pages, 27 figures; mistake is fixed in the last version;

papers.title: The gap persistence theorem for quantum multiparameter estimation
papers.abstract: One key aspect of quantum metrology, measurement incompatibility, is evident only through the simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters. The symmetric logarithmic derivative Cramer-Rao bound (SLDCRB), gives the attainable precision, if the optimal measurements for estimating each individual parameter commute with one another. As such, when the optimal measurements do not commute, the SLDCRB is not necessarily attainable. In this regard, the Holevo Cramer-Rao bound (HCRB) plays a fundamental role, providing the ultimate attainable precisions when one allows simultaneous measurements on infinitely many copies of a quantum state. For practical purposes, the Nagaoka Cramer-Rao bound (NCRB), or Nagaoka--Hayashi Cramer-Rao bound (NHCRB), is more relevant, as a lower bound when restricted to measuring quantum states individually. The interplay between these three bounds dictates how rapidly the ultimate metrological precisions can be approached through collective measurements on finite copies of the probe state. In this work we investigate this interplay. For full rank probe states, we prove that if the SLDCRB or HCRB cannot be saturated with measurements on a single copy of the probe state, then they cannot be saturated for any finite number of copies of the probe state. We demonstrate that these results do not necessarily hold for rank deficient states. As an application of this result, we show that it is impossible to saturate the HCRB for several physically motivated problems, including the simultaneous estimation of phase and phase diffusion. Finally, for practical purposes it is more relevant to study the rate at which the NHCRB converges to the HCRB. We prove that given $M$ copies of the probe state, the NHCRB converges to the HCRB at rate of at least $1/\sqrt{M}$.

papers.title: Para-fusion Category and Topological Defect Lines in $\mathbb Z_N$-parafermionic CFTs
papers.abstract: We study topological defect lines (TDLs) in two-dimensional $\mathbb Z_N$-parafermoinic CFTs. Different from the bosonic case, in the 2d parafermionic CFTs, there exist parafermionic defect operators that can live on the TDLs and satisfy interesting fractional statistics. We propose a categorical description for these TDLs, dubbed as ``para-fusion category", which contains various novel features, including $\mathbb Z_M$ $q$-type objects for $M\vert N$, and parafermoinic defect operators as a type of specialized 1-morphisms of the TDLs. The para-fusion category in parafermionic CFTs can be regarded as a natural generalization of the super-fusion category for the description of TDLs in 2d fermionic CFTs. We investigate these distinguishing features in para-fusion category from both a 2d pure CFT perspective, and also a 3d anyon condensation viewpoint. In the latter approach, we introduce a generalized parafermionic anyon condensation, and use it to establish a functor from the parent fusion category for TDLs in bosonic CFTs to the para-fusion category for TDLs in the parafermionized ones. At last, we provide many examples to illustrate the properties of the proposed para-fusion category, and also give a full classification for a universal para-fusion category obtained from parafermionic condensation of Tambara-Yamagami $\mathbb Z_N$ fusion category.

papers.title: Extended Set-based Tasks for Multi-task Execution and Prioritization
papers.abstract: The ability of executing multiple tasks simultaneously is an important feature of redundant robotic systems. As a matter of fact, complex behaviors can often be obtained as a result of the execution of several tasks. Moreover, in safety-critical applications, tasks designed to ensure the safety of the robot and its surroundings have to be executed along with other nominal tasks. In such cases, it is also important to prioritize the former over the latter. In this paper, we formalize the definition of extended set-based tasks, i.e., tasks which can be executed by rendering subsets of the task space asymptotically stable or forward invariant using control barrier functions. We propose a formal mathematical representation of such tasks that allows for the execution of more complex and time-varying prioritized stacks of tasks using kinematic and dynamic robot models alike. We present an optimization-based framework which is computationally efficient, accounts for input bounds, and allows for the stable execution of time-varying prioritized stacks of extended set-based tasks. The proposed framework is validated using extensive simulations, quantitative comparisons to the state-of-the-art hierarchical quadratic programming, and experiments with robotic manipulators.

papers.title: Elementary first-order model checking for sparse graphs
papers.abstract: It is known that for subgraph-closed graph classes the first-order model checking problem is fixed-parameter tractable if and only if the class is nowhere dense [Grohe, Kreutzer, Siebertz, 2017]. However, the dependency on the formula size is non-elementary, and in fact, this is unavoidable even for the class of all trees [Frick and Grohe, 2004]. On the other hand, it is known that the dependency is elementary for classes of bounded degree [Frick and Grohe, 2004] as well as for classes of bounded pathwidth [Lampis, 2026]. In this paper we generalise these results and almost completely characterise subgraph-closed graph classes for which the model checking problem is fixed-parameter tractable with an elementary dependency on the formula size. Those are the graph classes for which there exists a number $d$ such that for every $r$, some tree of depth $d$ and size bounded by an elementary function of $r$ is avoided as an $(\le r)$-subdivision in all graphs in the class. In particular, this implies that if the class in question excludes a fixed tree as a topological minor, then first-order model checking for graphs in the class is fixed-parameter tractable with an elementary dependency on the formula size.
papers.comments: 57 pages. This is the TheoretiCS journal version

papers.title: Asymmetry Amplification by a Nonadiabatic Passage through a Critical Point
papers.abstract: We propose and solve a minimal model of dynamic passage through a second-order phase transition in the presence of symmetry breaking interactions and no dissipation. Our model generalizes the Hamiltonian dynamics of the Painleve'-2 equation to the case with many degrees of freedom, while maintaining the integrability property. The evolution eventually leads to a highly asymmetric state, no matter how weak the symmetry breaking parameter of the Hamiltonian is. This suggests a potential mechanism for strong asymmetry in the production of quasi-particles with nearly identical characteristics. The model's integrability also yields exact exponents for the scaling of the density of the nonadiabatically excited quasi-particles.
papers.comments: 6 pages, 3 figures, last version corrected a few minor typos

papers.title: ProFL: Performative Robust Optimal Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Performative prediction is a framework that captures distribution shifts that occur during the training of machine learning models due to their deployment. As the trained model is used, the induced data distribution evolves, leading to deviations from the original data distribution. The impact of such model-induced distribution shifts in federated learning (FL) is increasingly likely to transpire in real-life use cases. A recently proposed approach extends performative prediction to FL with the resulting model converging to a performative stable point, which may be far from the performative optimal point. Earlier research in centralized settings has shown that the performative optimal point can be achieved under model-induced distribution shifts, but these approaches require the performative risk to be convex and the training data to be noiseless. These assumptions are often violated in realistic FL systems. This paper addresses these limitations and proposes Performative Robust Optimal Federated Learning (ProFL), an algorithm that targets the performative optimal point in FL while mitigating the effects of noisy and contaminated local data. We present a neighborhood-convergence analysis under the Polyak--Lojasiewicz condition, which applies to non-convex objectives. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the advantage of Robust Optimal Federated Learning over the state-of-the-art.
papers.comments: 27 pages, including appendices. Updated the theoretical analysis and experimental results to reflect the version accepted by IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing

papers.title: Bare-ancilla fault-tolerant syndrome extraction: General extensions of distance-three codes and structural criteria for graph codes
papers.abstract: The reliability of quantum computation critically depends on the performance of quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs). Performance of QECCs can be severely degraded by hook errors, which effectively reduce the code distance. We develop a systematic framework for bare-ancilla syndrome extraction in $[[n,k,3]]$ stabilizer codes. It provides a criterion for a specific single ancilla fault model and jointly searches for suitable stabilizer generators and data-ancilla interaction orders to correct hook errors. We call such stabilizer generator sets bare-ancilla codes (BACs). We also present two constructions that enlarge the set of valid BACs while preserving minimum distance, either by keeping the number of logical qubits fixed or by increasing it. Under the correlated-data error model, $3177$ $[[7,1,3]]$ graph codes are found to be BACs out of $3379$ and all $335415$ $[[8,1,3]]$ graph codes are BACs. We tested $500$ $[[7,1,3]]$ and $1000$ $[[8,1,3]]$ graph codes in the presence of anisotropic and depolarizing noise. The number of data-ancilla interactions is an important predictor of the pseudo-threshold of these graph codes. In the analyzed codes, the BAC, which works with the bare ancilla method, usually performs well or better than the flag method, particularly for depolarizing noise. Notably, we report new bare ancilla codes, namely $[[6,1,3]]$ and $[[7,1,3]]$ with improved code rate compared to the bare code used in the work of Muyuan Li \emph{et al.} and Maheshwari \emph{et al.} respectively.

papers.title: Sequential Monte Carlo approximations of Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao gradient flows
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of sampling from a probability distribution $π$. It is well known that this can be written as an optimisation problem over the space of probability distribution in which we aim to minimise the Kullback--Leibler divergence from $π$. We consider several partial differential equations (PDEs) whose solution is a minimiser of the Kullback--Leibler divergence from $π$ and connect them to well-known Monte Carlo algorithms. We focus in particular on PDEs obtained by considering the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao geometry over the space of probabilities and show that these lead to a natural implementation using importance sampling and sequential Monte Carlo. We propose a novel algorithm to approximate the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao flow of the Kullback--Leibler divergence and conduct an extensive empirical study to identify when this algorithm outperforms other popular Monte Carlo algorithms.
papers.comments: Changes from v1: the study of tempered dynamics was removed in favour of a larger experimental section

papers.title: Perfect Clustering in Extremely Sparse Multilayer Networks with Groupwise Subspace Structure
papers.abstract: The paper studies a multilayer network on the same collection of nodes, where each layer follows the Generalized Random Dot Product Graph Model. Furthermore, all layers can be partitioned into groups, each group with its own unique latent subspace structure, but otherwise the matrices of connection probabilities can all be different. This setting is extremely general and includes most multilayer network models as special cases. In addition, we are interested in the situation where the layer networks may be extremely sparse and, therefore, the layer-by-layer analysis is unreliable. This problem can also be seen as a generalization of the classic setting in which one recovers a shared structure across an entire collection of matrices, extending it to the case where such structures are shared only within specific groups of matrices. The key task in this setting is to recover the groups of layers with unique subspace structures, since, after that, the information in those groups of layers can be pooled together by well-studied methods. Until now, clustering of layers in such networks was based on layer-by-layer analysis, which required the multilayer network to be sufficiently dense. Our paper is the first to provide a tensor-based approach to the problem that combines information from all layers in an unconventional manner. Our theoretical results, established under intuitive and non-restrictive assumptions, assert that the new technique achieves perfect clustering under sparsity conditions that, up to logarithmic factors, coincide with the computational lower bound derived for a much simpler model. The paper also delivers a nuanced message about the applicability of the new technique.

papers.title: A JT/KPZ correspondence
papers.abstract: We point out a correspondence between the Jackiw--Teitelboim (JT) gravity and the stationary measure of the Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation on an interval. By relating the Schwarzian limit of the double-scaled SYK to the weakly asymmetric limit of the open ASEP, we establish that the path-integral measure defining the Euclidean evolution between two end-of-the-world branes in JT gravity can be interpreted as the stationary measure of the KPZ equation on an interval with Neumann boundary conditions. We also establish the match between correlation functions.

papers.title: Topological subregions in Chern Simons theory and topological string theory
papers.abstract: The standard, gapped entanglement boundary condition in Chern Simons theory breaks the topological invariance of the theory by introducing a complex structure on the entangling surface. This produces an infinite dimensional subregion Hilbert space, a non-trivial modular Hamiltonion, and a UV-divergent entanglement entropy that is a universal feature of local quantum field theories. In this work, we appeal to the combinatorial quantization of Chern Simons theory to define a purely topological notion of a subregion. The subregion operator algebras are spaces of functions on a quantum group. We develop a diagrammatic calculus for the associated $q$-deformed entanglement entropy, which arise from the entanglement of anyonic edge modes. The $q$-deformation regulates the divergences of the QFT, producing a finite entanglement entropy associated to a $q$-tracial state. We explain how these ideas provide an operator algebraic framework for the entanglement entropy computations in topological string theory \cite{Donnelly:2020teo,Jiang:2020cqo, wongtopstring}, where a large- $N$ limit of the $q$-deformed subregion algebra plays a key role in the stringy description of spacetime.
papers.comments: Section 2-4 substantially revised. Section 2 contains a new derivation of the modular Hamiltonian for a topological subregion. Section 3 now defines classical subregions using the Fock-Rosly phase space

papers.title: Exact general solutions for cosmological scalar field evolution in a vacuum-energy dominated expansion
papers.abstract: We derive exact general solutions (as opposed to attractor particular solutions) for the evolution of a scalar field $φ$ in a universe dominated by a background fluid with equation of state parameter $w_B = -1$, extending earlier work on exact solutions with $w_B > -1$. Straightfoward exact solutions exist when the evolution is described by a linear differential equation, corresponding to constant, linear, and quadratic potentials. In the nonlinear case, exact solutions are derived for $V = V_0\ln φ$, $V = V_0 φ^{1/2}$ and $V = V_0/φ$, and the logarithmic potential also yields an exact first integral. These complicated parametric solutions are considerably less useful than those derived previously for a universe dominated by a barotropic fluid such as matter or radiation with $w_B > -1$. However, we generalize the slow-roll approximation and show that it applies to all sufficiently flat potentials in the case of a vacuum-dominated expansion, while it never applies when the universe is dominated by a background fluid with $w_B > -1$.
papers.comments: 10 pages, 1 figure, discussion, references, and phase-plane figure added, submitted to IJMPD

papers.title: Single-valued flat connections in several variables on arbitrary Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: Polylogarithms on Riemann surfaces may be constructed systematically in terms of flat connections that can enjoy various algebraic and analytic properties. In this paper, we present a single-valued and modular invariant connection ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ on the configuration space $\text{Cf}_n(Σ)$ of an arbitrary number $n$ of points on an arbitrary compact Riemann surface $Σ$ with or without punctures. The connection ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ generalizes an earlier construction for a single variable and is built out of the same integration kernels. We show that ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ is flat on $\text{Cf}_n(Σ)$. For the case without punctures, we relate it to the meromorphic multiple-valued Enriquez connection ${\cal K}_\text{E}$ in $n$ variables on the universal cover $\tilde Σ$ of $Σ$ by the composition of a gauge transformation and an automorphism of the Lie algebra in which ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ and ${\cal K}_\text{E}$ take values. In a companion paper, we shall establish the equivalence between the flatness of these connections and the corresponding interchange and Fay identities, for arbitrary compact Riemann surfaces.
papers.comments: 46+37 pages, v2: clarifications and minor corrections, matches published version

papers.title: Instance-optimal high-precision shadow tomography with few-copy measurements: A metrological approach
papers.abstract: We study the sample complexity of shadow tomography in the high-precision regime under realistic measurement constraints. Given an unknown $d$-dimensional quantum state $ρ$ and a known set of observables $\{O_i\}_{i=1}^m$, the goal is to estimate expectation values $\{\mathrm{tr}(O_iρ)\}_{i=1}^m$ to accuracy $ε$ in $L_p$-norm, using possibly adaptive measurements that act on $O(\mathrm{polylog}(d))$ number of copies of $ρ$ at a time. We focus on the regime where $ε$ is below an instance-dependent threshold. Our main contribution is an instance-optimal characterization of the sample complexity as $\tildeΘ(Γ_p/ε^2)$, where $Γ_p$ is a function of $\{O_i\}_{i=1}^m$ defined via an optimization formula involving the inverse Fisher information matrix. Previously, tight bounds were known only in special cases, e.g. Pauli shadow tomography with $L_\infty$-norm error. Concretely, we first analyze a simpler oblivious variant where the goal is to estimate an observable of the form $\sum_{i=1}^m α_i O_i$ with $\|α\|_q = 1$ (where $q$ is dual to $p$) revealed after the measurement. For single-copy measurements, we obtain a sample complexity of $Θ(Γ^{\mathrm{ob}}_p/ε^2)$. We then show $\tildeΘ(Γ_p/ε^2)$ is necessary and sufficient for the original problem, with the lower bound applying to unbiased, kurtosis-bounded estimators when $p \geq 1$. Our upper bounds rely on a two-step algorithm combining coarse tomography with local estimation. Notably, $Γ^{\mathrm{ob}}_\infty = Γ_\infty$. In both cases, allowing $c$-copy measurements improves the sample complexity by at most $Ω(1/c)$. Our results establish a quantitative correspondence between quantum learning and metrology, unifying asymptotic metrological limits with finite-sample learning guarantees.
papers.comments: 69 pages; several technical errors from the earlier version fixed including the wrong order of optimization over measurements and references states; key messages remain unchanged
papers.journal_ref: Proceedings of Thirty Ninth Conference on Learning Theory, PMLR 336:1115-1185, 2026

papers.title: Spin chains for ADE quiver theories
papers.abstract: The spectral problem of four-dimensional superconformal quiver gauge theories can be mapped to one-dimensional spin chains with restricted Hilbert spaces, where the composition of neighbouring spins follows the path algebra of the quiver. To better understand such spin chains, we compute the one-loop planar dilatation operator for the 4d N=2 ADE quiver gauge theories obtained by orbifolding the N=4 Super-Yang-Mills theory and marginally deforming by independently varying the gauge couplings. This extends previous work which was mainly focused on the Z2 quiver. We characterise the general features of the resulting ADE spin-chain models and construct the 2-magnon Bethe ansatz for holomorphic states. We also evaluate, at large N, the N=2 superconformal index of these gauge theories and use it to study their protected spectrum in specific sectors.
papers.comments: 92 pages + appendices. Based on an MSc dissertation to be submitted by the first author to the University of Pretoria. v2: Published version

papers.title: Uniform Maximum Projection Designs for Computer Experiments
papers.abstract: Space-filling experimental designs are widely used in engineering computer experiments, where only a limited number of expensive model evaluations can be afforded. Distance-based designs such as Maximin or Minimax ensure global space-filling, while Latin hypercube sampling enforces uniform one-dimensional projections, yet neither guarantees uniformity in lowdimensional subspaces. Maximum Projection (MaxPro) designs were introduced to improve uniformity in low-dimensional subspaces, yet their original formulation relies on the Euclidean distance and may induce systematic density distortions in bounded domains. We demonstrate that the standard MaxPro criterion leads to statistically non-uniform sampling, resulting in undersampling of corner regions and biased Monte Carlo estimates. To remedy this issue, we introduce a periodic variant of the criterion, termed Uniform Maximum Projection (uMaxPro), in which the Euclidean metric is replaced by a periodic distance based on the minimum image convention. The proposed uMaxPro designs preserve the projection-aware structure of MaxPro while achieving statistical uniformity of the design-generation mechanism. Numerical experiments show unbiased Monte Carlo integration with reduced variance, excellent subspace projection performance, and competitive discrepancy properties. The methodology is further validated on benchmark engineering problems, including a meso-scale finite element model of concrete, demonstrating improved accuracy in surrogate modeling and probabilistic estimation. The resulting criterion provides a simple and computationally efficient modification of MaxPro that enhances its robustness for nonadaptive computer experiments. The construction algorithm, open-source implementation, and reproducible optimized designs are provided to facilitate practical adoption of the method.

papers.title: Soft projections for robust data-driven control
papers.abstract: We consider data-based predictive control based on behavioral systems theory. In the linear setting this means that a system is described as a subspace of trajectories, and predictive control can be formulated using a projection onto the intersection of this behavior and a constraint set. Instead of learning the model, or subspace, we focus on determining this projection from data. Motivated by the use of regularization in data-enabled predictive control (DeePC), we introduce the use of soft projections, which approximate the true projector onto the behavior from noisy data. In the simplest case, these are equivalent to known regularized DeePC schemes, but they exhibit a number of benefits. First, we provide a bound on the approximation error consisting of a bias and a variance term that can be traded-off by the regularization weight. The derived bound is independent of the true system order, highlighting the benefit of soft projections compared to low-dimensional subspace estimates. Moreover, soft projections allow for intuitive generalizations, one of which we show has superior performance on a case study. Finally, we provide update formulas for soft projectors enabling the efficient adaptation of the proposed data-driven control methods in the case of streaming data.

papers.title: Learning Cut Distributions with Quantum Optimization
papers.abstract: The probabilistic nature of quantum computation can be an asset rather than an obstacle for combinatorial optimization. In this work, we tackle the problem in which the sampled distribution itself is the object being optimized. This perspective is especially natural for fairness, coverage, and robustness objectives, where success is determined by the least-protected components rather than by average or best performance. We develop this idea by learning graph cut distributions. The resulting framework turns Fair Cut Cover into a native quantum distribution-learning problem and uses quantum circuits as trainable generators of cut distributions. We prove that standard QAOA at depth one achieves higher Fair Cut Cover values than optimal Semidefinite programming plus Gaussian hyperplane rounding on complete graphs with at least four vertices. We further establish a separation on a family of high-girth graphs using published QAOA evaluations, compare against a classical column-generation heuristic in numerical experiments, and examine finite-sampling and noise effects in quantum hardware implementations. These results suggest a broader role for this type of quantum algorithms: not merely finding good bitstrings, but learning useful combinatorial distributions for worst- and average-case-aware optimization.

papers.title: Tube-Based Robust Data-Driven Predictive Control for Linear Time-Invariant Systems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a tractable tube-based robust data-driven predictive control scheme that uses only a single finite noisy input-state trajectory of an unknown discrete-time linear time-invariant (LTI) system. A simplex constraint is imposed on the Hankel coefficient vector, yielding explicit polyhedral bounds on the prediction mismatch induced by bounded measurement noise. Using certified initial and terminal robust positively invariant (RPI) sets, we derive a tube-tightened formulation whose online optimization problem is a strictly convex quadratic program (QP). The resulting controller guarantees recursive feasibility, robust satisfaction of input and state constraints, and practical input-to-state stability of the closed loop with respect to measurement noise. Numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness, robustness, and closed-loop performance of the proposed method.

papers.title: Quantum Fisher Information and Separable Energy Minima in Spin Systems
papers.abstract: We develop a general method to bound the minimum energy of spin Hamiltonians over separable states with fixed single-particle reduced density matrices. The method uses a two-particle optimization and identifies conditions under which the resulting bound is tight. For ferromagnetic Ising and Ising-like interactions on any regular graph, we obtain an exact separable-energy minimum expressed through the quantum Fisher information (QFI) of the local state; a symmetric separable state attains the optimal correlation on every bond. For fully connected ferromagnetic Ising-like systems, ground-state correlations give a lower estimate of this single-particle QFI with a rigorous O(1/N) finite-size error. Further exact results relate symmetric-separable minima of antiferromagnetic Ising-like and XY-like models to local expectation values, and ferromagnetic spin-1/2 Heisenberg chains to quantum fidelity. We also derive bounds for separability across fixed partitions into contiguous blocks.

papers.title: Minimum-Length Permutation-Invariant Qudit Codes from Edge-Colorings of Complete Graphs
papers.abstract: We study permutation-invariant quantum codes in the symmetric subspace $\mathrm{Sym}^n(\mathbb{C}^q)$ of $n$ qudits of local dimension $q$. For every integer $q\ge 2$, we construct a permutation-invariant code with parameters $((4,q,2))_q$. Thus four physical qudits suffice to encode one logical qudit with distance two in the symmetric sector for every local dimension. We also show, using a self-contained decoupling and rank argument, that no permutation-invariant code of dimension $q$ and distance at least $2$ exists in $\mathrm{Sym}^n(\mathbb{C}^q)$ for $n\le 3$. Hence four qudits are necessary and sufficient. The construction has simple representation-theoretic and combinatorial descriptions. On $\mathrm{Sym}^4(\mathbb{C}^q)$, the distance-two Knill--Laflamme conditions split into root and Cartan parts. By restricting supports to the even-entry occupation layer, all root-error conditions vanish automatically. The remaining Cartan conditions reduce to linear balancing constraints on packets of occupation vectors. These packets admit a natural graph-theoretic interpretation in terms of the vertices and edges of the complete graph $K_q$: for odd $q$, they are organized by the midpoint rule, while for even $q$, they are organized by a decomposition of $K_q$ into perfect matchings. In this way, the existence of minimum-length $((4,q,2))_q$ permutation-invariant codes is reduced to a parity-dependent edge-coloring problem on $K_q$.
papers.comments: 17 pages, 1 figure. Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Information Theory. Added a self-contained proof of the minimum block length, expanded the discussion of physical motivation and prior work, and improved the exposition

papers.title: Endowing phase-field fracture models with custom strength criteria
papers.abstract: By now, several approaches have been proposed to endow phase-field fracture models with the ability to describe crack nucleation under multiaxial stress states. These include techniques for splitting the free energy, direct modifications of the phase-field driving or resisting forces, and the introduction of additional internal variables, such as plastic strains or other nonlinear strains. In this paper, we propose a fundamentally different strategy for incorporating arbitrary elastic domains into phase-field fracture models, formulated within the energetic framework of generalized standard materials. The proposed approach relies on letting the dissipation potential depend on the current state of the material. In this way, the elastic degradation and the strength criterion remain two distinct and independently controllable aspects of the material response, while the governing equations directly descend from a local stability condition and energy balance. Simple yet representative models are presented and thoroughly discussed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology. The resulting evolution of the elastic domain is investigated in both strain and stress spaces under proportional and non-proportional loading paths, with the latter highlighting the path dependence of the dissipated work. Moreover, numerical simulations demonstrate a range of crack nucleation processes under multiaxial loading conditions for various analytical strength surfaces. The present work paves the way for future developments and applications in several directions, including crack propagation studies and dedicated numerical solution strategies.

papers.title: Quantum Computing Algebra (QCA), the theory and implementation
papers.abstract: We present a real geometric algebra framework designed for the direct translation of the Dirac formalism into geometric algebra representations. Unlike previous approaches based on positive-definite signatures, QCA employs a split-signature construction that enables a natural realization of quantum states and operators while simplifying computational implementation. We further present an implementation of QCA using the \textit{GAALOP} software and show how quantum gates and multi-qubit systems can be efficiently represented and generated computationally. As an application, we demonstrate the use of QCA in quantum game theory, where the real-algebraic formulation provides computational advantages for modeling entangled strategies and quantum interactions. The proposed framework establishes a practical bridge between the abstract formalism of quantum computation and efficient geometric algebra implementations.

papers.title: LLM-ACES: Closed-Loop Discovery of Dynamical Systems with LLM-Guided Adaptive Search
papers.abstract: Recovering governing ordinary differential equations (ODEs) from data is a central challenge in modeling dynamical systems across scientific domains. Existing approaches cast discovery as a static inference problem over fixed datasets, assuming that the observed trajectories are sufficiently informative. However, dynamical systems evolve over large state spaces, and limited data can make multiple equations observationally indistinguishable, leading to identifiability gaps and the recovery of incorrect governing equations. To address this, we introduce LLM-ACES, or LLM-guided Active Closed-loop Equation Search, a closed-loop framework that jointly optimizes symbolic hypothesis construction and adaptive data acquisition. In LLM-ACES, a large language model (LLM) proposes operator priors that define constrained subspaces of the symbolic search space, within which candidate equations are fit to the observed data. The disagreement among these candidates guides the acquisition of informative trajectories, creating a feedback loop that iteratively refines both the hypothesis space and the discovered dynamics. On 122 ODE systems spanning ODEBench and ODEBase, LLM-ACES achieves the lowest median NMSE, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines while reaching the highest symbolic accuracy up to 70.8% on ODEBench and 69.5% on ODEBase across different LLM backbones. Our analysis further shows that LLM-ACES is sample-efficient, achieving better performance with less data. Under observation noise and sparse sampling, LLM-ACES keeps the lowest reconstruction error without inflating expression complexity, whereas baselines tend to add spurious terms that fit the data locally but obscure the governing relationships. Code: https://github.com/scientific-discovery/LLM-ACES

papers.title: A Unified Heat-Ball Framework for Fokker--Planck Equations: Mean-Value Identities, Exact Sampling, and Error Analysis
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based generative models with nonlinear or learned forward drifts raise questions that stay hidden for Gaussian forward processes: how the divergence-free and gradient parts of the drift shape the evolving density, whether sampling can draw on local rather than global information, and how to treat low-density regions, where $u$ carries a weak signal while $\log u$ diverges and the entropy density $u\log u$ falls between the two. These questions motivate the present study of local representations for Fokker--Planck equations with general, possibly nonlinear and time-dependent drift. We derive inhomogeneous heat-ball identities for the density $u$, the log-density $\log u$, the entropy density $u\log u$, and the score $\nabla\log u$, keeping the source terms generated by the drift; their unscaled residuals recover the corresponding differential residuals at leading order in the squared heat-ball radius. The weights appearing in the identities, the source integrals, and the integration-by-parts formulas all belong to a single Beta--Gamma family of measures on the heat ball, which gives exact rejection-free sampling, product quadrature, and unbiased Monte Carlo estimators with variance and cost bounds that are explicit in the dimension and the radius. Experiments with Gaussian-mixture and nonlinear-drift references, in dimensions up to $1024$ where applicable, confirm the sampling laws, the identities, and the residual behavior. In particular, log-density and score evaluations remain accurate where direct density estimation breaks down, and the heat-ball residuals provide local consistency tests for learned score models. A study of gauge-based heat-ball walks illustrates a recursive use of the density identity.

papers.title: Parameter-Free Dynamic Regret under Heavy-Tailed Noise
papers.abstract: We study online convex optimization on a compact convex domain of diameter $D$ in which the learner observes, at each round, one stochastic subgradient and no loss values. The observations are conditionally unbiased, and the noise has an unconditional $p$-th moment at most $σ^p$ for an unknown $p\in(1,2]$; for $p<2$ its variance may be infinite. For a comparator sequence of path length $P_T$ we write $Λ_T=1+P_T/D$, and we show that the minimax expected dynamic regret is, up to numerical constants, \[ \min\Bigl\{GD\sqrt{TΛ_T}+σDT^{1/p}Λ_T^{(p-1)/p},\ GDT\Bigr\}, \] where $G$ bounds the subgradients. The lower bound holds on every compact convex domain of positive diameter. An algorithm that combines AdaGrad learners restarted at different frequencies through exponential weights with a data-dependent learning rate attains this rate for each fixed $p>1$, without knowing $G$, $σ$, $p$, or $P_T$: the constant of the first term is numerical, the constant of the second is $O(1+\log(p/(p-1)))$, and no logarithmic factor of $T$ appears. The analysis bounds the gradient energy separately on each restart block, which gives the exponent $(p-1)/p$ of $Λ_T$ in the noise term; a bound over the whole horizon gives the exponent $1/2$. Running the algorithm on epochs of doubling length removes the need to know $T$ at the cost of a factor $2+\sqrt2$. The appendices give a high-probability version and a synthetic study.

papers.title: Constrained Online Learning with Noisy Constraint Values
papers.abstract: We study online convex optimization with time-varying constraints when the constraint values are observed only through noise. In each round the learner picks an action, pays a convex loss, and incurs a convex constraint value that should be nonpositive; it then receives unbiased estimates of the loss and constraint gradients, and an unbiased observation of the constraint value whose error has bounded variance. Performance is measured against the best fixed action in hindsight among those that satisfy every constraint, and violation by the largest total overspend over any interval of consecutive rounds, which we call budget violation. Our algorithm, LEDGER, has $O(\sqrt T)$ expected regret and $O(\sqrt{T\log T})$ expected budget violation over $T$ rounds, uses one projection per round, and needs no strictly feasible action. The logarithm cannot be removed: with Gaussian noise of fixed positive variance, every algorithm with $O(\sqrt T)$ worst-case regret has worst-case budget violation of order at least $\sqrt{T\log T}$, even if only the final total overspend is counted, and budget violation $O(\sqrt T)$ forces linear regret. When violation is instead the sum of the positive parts of the per-round constraint values (hard violation), no algorithm keeps both expected regret and expected hard violation sublinear if the noise distribution is not fixed, even for affine constraints. With a fixed and known Gaussian noise law of standard deviation $σ$, a worst-case lower bound of order $\min\{σ,1\}T(\log\log T/\log T)^2$ shows that regret and hard violation cannot both be made polynomially sublinear. Noisy constraint values therefore still allow a signed budget to be controlled, at the cost of a logarithmic factor, but not the hard violation.

papers.title: Indistinguishability Theory for Identical Particles with Invariant Degrees of Freedom
papers.abstract: Identical particles have dynamically invariant labels in all setups where their degrees of freedom can be partitioned into two parts, which we call internal and visible, with the visible part subject to unitary evolution, while the dynamically invariant internal part accounts for the partial distinguishability of particles. We give the explicit form of the visible state in terms of the indistinguishability function, generalizing the standard symmetrization/antisymmetrization postulate for bosons/fermions with internal modes. The indistinguishability function on the symmetric group accounts for the permutation symmetry of the dynamically invariant label state and gives a self-contained description of the symmetry spectrum of the visible state. It is shown that the indistinguishability of single particles emitted independently from a stable source is completely characterized by the projective measures on the symmetry spectrum. We reveal a hierarchy of successive upper bounds on the projective measure of indistinguishability in terms of marginal projective measures. We point out an experimentally feasible way to get the upper bounds on the indistinguishability of an arbitrarily large number of single photons by direct experimental readout of their marginal projective measures. We also analyze the indistinguishability of coherent superpositions and convex mixtures and resolve a recently posed problem.
papers.comments: 27 pages, no figures; two references added in the revision

papers.title: Exponential Smoothing for Time Series of Random Objects
papers.abstract: Time series of random objects, such as covariance matrices, probability distributions, and functional data, call for forecasting methods that do not rely on arithmetic operations. We introduce geodesic exponential smoothing for time series in Hadamard spaces. The forecast level moves a fixed fraction of the way along the geodesic towards each new observation. The smoothing parameter is estimated by minimising the average squared distance between observations and forecasts. The method involves a single scalar parameter, assumes no stationarity, and updates online in constant time per observation. We further introduce an innovations mechanism under which each observation has conditional Fréchet mean equal to the current level, the metric-space analogue of the innovations state-space model. We show via the quasilinearisation of Hadamard spaces that the level is a martingale in a nonlinear sense, that the spread of the data from the initial state grows at least linearly in time, and that their quasi-autocorrelation at any fixed lag tends to one. We prove almost-sure consistency and asymptotic normality of the smoothing-parameter estimator. Three real-data applications, spanning covariance-matrix, distributional, and functional time series, assess the forecasting performance against structurally heavier alternatives.

papers.title: Formulation-dependent linearized buckling of stiffened shell panels: role of the stress stiffness operator
papers.abstract: Linearized buckling loads of stiffened panels can diverge across commercial shell formulations because six-degree-of-freedom elements treat drilling rotations and director kinematics differently in the stress stiffness operator. We derive three analytical stress stiffness operators (membrane-only, uncoupled rotational-block, and shear-coupled full second-variation forms), verified against an exact second-difference energy identity. Using direct matrix extraction in ANSYS (SHELL181, SHELL281) and modal and strain-energy benchmarks in Abaqus (S4, S8R), we classify these commercial elements across twelve configurations. On the finest cantilevered shear-panel mesh (in-plane bending and shear), the SHELL181 perturbation and classic procedures predict load factors 11.3% and 28.5% above an independent 3D continuum reference. By contrast, Abaqus S4 and ANSYS SHELL281 lie 5.2% and 5.8% below this reference and remain indistinguishable from the analytical full form within the junction-idealization uncertainty, while Abaqus S8R lies 20.1% below the reference. The tested cases indicate that substantial divergence occurs only when non-coplanar junctions carry pre-stress bending or transverse shear and the buckling mode involves junction drilling rotations. Under pure axial compression or uniform membrane shear flow, the analytical operators coincide and within-element procedures agree within 0.06%. Because buckling under in-plane bending and shear is formulation-dependent, stability design and layout optimization of built-up panels require cross-verification across shell elements or continuum models.
papers.comments: 26 pages, 9 figures, 16 tables. Major revision following peer review: revised title, comprehensive language and structural rewrite, reorganized Results section, and added through-thickness 3D continuum refinement study

papers.title: When Hedging Changes the Payoff: Option Replication with Price Impact and Execution Costs
papers.abstract: Hedging a derivative by trading the underlying asset changes the payoff that the hedging intended to replicate. We study this phenomenon when trading generates price impact and execution costs. In a binomial model, we characterize replication through a fixed point equation. In continuous time, we derive a nonlinear pricing PDE whose implicit terminal condition captures the nature of the moving target problem of the hedger. For monotone convex Lipschitz payoffs (such as calls and puts) we establish exact replication under midpoint execution costs. Numerical experiments illustrate: (i) how price impact shifts the effective strike, (ii) the nonlinear dependence of the option price on the number of contracts, (iii) how execution costs smooth terminal holdings, (iv) the extent to which the hedger's own trading can bring an otherwise worthless option into the money, and (v) how the spread and the shape of the limit order book in the options market arise from the price impact and the shape of the limit order book of the underlying. In particular, calibrating the one-period binomial model to trade and quote data on near-expiry SPY call options, we find that our model explains 85\% of the observed option bid-ask spread for near-the-money options.

papers.title: Antipodal Self-Duality for Generalized Fishnets from Integrability
papers.abstract: Antipodal self-duality (ASD) is a remarkable property that relates an amplitude to itself, after performing a suitable kinematic map and reversing the letters of the symbol (more precisely, acting with the antipode of the Hopf algebra of the de Rham analogs of multiple polylogarithms). ASD has been seen in only one process in planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory, and its physical origin is unknown, motivating a search for ASD in other contexts. Recently, ASD was found to hold for square fishnet integrals in a strongly-deformed version of planar $\mathcal{N}=4$. In this paper, we investigate the properties of polynomials in ladder integrals under the ASD transformation that leaves the square fishnet invariant. Our basic building blocks are determinants of certain matrices of ladder integrals, that are labeled by partitions or Young diagrams, and automatically obey the Steinmann relations. We employ integrability-based representations of such determinants, which are essentially matrix-model integrals, and the theory of symmetric polynomials to find many more ASD quantities -- linear combinations of determinants whose coefficients are expressed using the combinatorics of partitions. As a byproduct, we provide an alternate proof that square fishnet integrals obey ASD.
papers.comments: 28 pages, 3 figures; v2: de Rham disclaimer and minor corrections

papers.title: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
papers.abstract: We study equilibration of a fixed subsystem coupled to an initially maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square error, maximised over observation windows of length $T$, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation on $[0,T]$. The constants depend only on the subsystem dimension, and no assumption on degeneracies of energies or energy gaps is required. Subtracting the stationary part of the correlation gives equilibration to the temporal state; retaining it gives thermalisation to the maximally mixed state. We then obtain explicit bounds for two static Hamiltonian families. A periodic spin-clock model thermalises on $O(n\log n)$ windows at fixed accuracy despite an exponentially small positive energy. A randomly dressed commuting model, with interaction range $O(\log N)$, has expected error $O(N^{-b}+T^{-1})$ while retaining an extensive family of conserved observables. We explain how the locally weighted spectrum determines these bounds.
papers.comments: comments welcome; 9 pages main plus 16 supplementary, 2 figures, v2: substantially rewritten version with new results, v3: updated version with clearer presentation, v4: some minor clarification and more comprehensive supplementary note

papers.title: Ramanujan Challenge Results: AI-Assisted Evaluation Pipeline for Multi-Format Proofs
papers.abstract: As AI's mathematical capabilities rapidly improve, meaningful benchmarks are shifting from university-level problems and math olympiads to research-level mathematics. The Ramanujan Challenge is a benchmark comprised of research-level problems in number theory, including unpublished results and open conjectures. It presented concrete formulas for mathematical constants whose correctness can be checked numerically, while their proofs may require non-obvious mathematics. Here, we analyze the Challenge submissions, measuring the relative success of different AI models, Computer Algebra Systems (CAS), and formal tools. We find correct submissions that are conceptually distinct from the official solutions, and a proof of one of the published open conjectures. Evaluating the submissions exposed a second challenge: judging complex proofs reliably at scale. We introduce an AI-assisted evaluation pipeline for natural language proofs, CAS code, and Lean formalizations that assesses semantic and logical correctness. Compared with the conventional one-shot LLM judgment, our pipeline reduces false-positive verdicts on natural language proofs from 23% to 6% and improves judgment accuracy on supporting code from 46% to 58%. This approach provides a methodology for evaluating research-level mathematics at scale, with potential applications across mathematics and AI for science.

papers.title: Bondi-Sachs formalism on past light cones and an analogue of the integral mass formula
papers.abstract: Following a proposal that the thermodynamic aspects of general relativity can be found in the evolution of the past light cones of arbitrary worldlines, we generalise the Bondi-Sachs formalism to these surfaces. The observer may accelerate and rotate their tetrad, the spacetime may contain matter and a cosmological constant, and no symmetry is assumed. We impose regularity conditions at the vertex of each light cone and along the polar axis, including general axial conditions that allow for shear. Given a suitable prescription for the stresses of matter, the Einstein field equations can then be integrated hierarchically from data on a single light cone, and the regularity at the vertex fixes all constants of integration. The solution reveals a universal property: to first order in the observer's proper time, the evolution of the metric and of the four-momentum crossing the light cones is independent of the specific behaviour of matter. As an application, we derive, for an observer immersed in matter, an analogue of the integral mass formula of black hole mechanics.
papers.comments: 31 pages, 2 figures. Presents part of the results of arXiv:2609.25477. v2: improved treatment of the axial conditions and minor corrections

papers.title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
papers.abstract: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound. However, local algebras in relativistic quantum field theory are of type III: they carry no trace, so that states are not described by density matrices in the algebra, and they have no pure normal states, such that the SLD quantum Fisher information and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound cannot be defined in the usual way. We define the SLD (Bures) quantum Fisher information on arbitrary von Neumann algebras through Uhlmann's transition probability and prove a quantum Cramér--Rao bound for collective measurements. We also show that the bound is sharp, and equals the largest classical Fisher information obtainable by measurements in the region.

papers.title: Certificate-Based Verification of Pulsed Field Ablation Models
papers.abstract: Computational models of cardiac pulsed field ablation predict the lesion as the tissue where the electric field exceeds a lethal threshold. Their numerical error is rarely bounded, and automated pipelines increasingly run them without an expert checking each result. To verify each run, we separate the question "was the stated model solved correctly?" from the solver that answers it. An untrusted solver returns its answer with a certificate, which consists of a potential with the correct electrode and ground values and an exactly charge-conserving current. A small independent checker verifies the certificate against a written specification of the physics. Using the Prager-Synge hypercircle theorem evaluated in ball arithmetic, it turns the certificate into guaranteed two-sided bounds on the impedance and on the root-mean-square field of every tile of a lesion map, also over a range of blood/tissue conductivity ratios. The bounds cover numerical error only; whether the model describes tissue is a question of validation. A vectorized version of the checker takes about a tenth of our solver's time. For a focal electrode in contact, the tile-resolved depth at 1000 V and 700 V/cm is proven to lie in 3.50-3.75 mm for every ratio from 1.7 to 3.75. For a bipolar catheter, certified depths overlap published in-vivo depths. Where they differ from a published reference model, the certificates prove that the difference is not our numerical error. We compare the certificate with a grid convergence study on the same solver. On graded grids, the study is sharper for local fields but remains an estimate. On uniform grids, it fails to converge at the electrode edge, where the certificate still gives a valid bracket. Solvers that deliberately solve equations other than the specified ones pass the grid convergence study, but the certificates refute the impedances they report or leave them unsupported.

papers.title: Localization identities for spectral determinants: two-dimensional QCD and Ising field theory
papers.abstract: Spectral determinants encode the meson spectra of planar two-dimensional QCD and of Ising field theory in the two-particle Bethe-Salpeter approximation.
